GovTextLoss: Your loss has put our planet in a very difficult position, <Player>. Now we will have to tolerate the presence of these machines for another three months. Needless to say, we won't be paying you anything, so you may go.

Then again, <Player>, I've got some good news for you, too. Our government has allocated a sum of <Money> cr to all of our planet's guests, so that they could buy themselves special anti-disodane suits. This money has already been transferred to your account. That's how it goes sometimes: some suffer, while others make out like bandits.
GovTextStart: Ranger <Player>, we need your help.

After our system was liberated from the dominators, on some planets these death machines continue to multiply. The Galactic Council has promised to send in troops only in three months, but we cannot afford to wait that long, not with our people living in constant danger.

We know that fighting dominators on planets isn't part of ranger responsibilities; nevertheless, we must ask you to help us liquidate these robots. The cleansing operation is top-secret in order to prevent widespread panic on planet <Planet>, so we can fill you in on the details only after you accept this mission.
GovTextWin: Dear <Player>, we've got the disodane! We want to thank you for not staying indifferent to the fate of planet <Planet> and helping us at the risk to your own life.

Our government has allocated a huge monetary reward for you, but, unfortunately, the ranger center thought that this would put you in an unfair position to the other rangers. It was therefore decided to split the reward among 20 most outstanding rangers. This means that you will only receive one twentieth of the initial amount due to you -- <Money> cr. You can easily calculate the full amount... but that's no longer important.
01.Name: Desert Disodane
RobotsLoss: You have surrendered all strategically important positions, <Player>. Where's our disodane now?!!
You are expected to report to the government building. Be there.
RobotsStart: Here's the lowdown:

You are part of a secret operation codenamed <clr>"Desert Disodane"<clrEnd>. The dominators are interested in this particular region of our planet due to massive disodane deposits located there. Have you heard anything about it? Actually, never mind, this information is classified.

The point is that, evidently, the robots want to start mining it. Obviously, we have no idea what their end goal is, but the mere fact that Blazeroids, Kelleroids and Terronoids are contesting a scrap of land is disconcerting. What happens when one side emerges as the winner? One thing is clear: that side must be us!

Now, thanks to a fortunate concurrence of circumstances we've managed to capture a base and even build a small detachment of robots. Of course, these robots are not intelligent but are being operated via control units, including manual control. With these resources at hand, you must capture all of the enemy's factories.
Now go, <Player>, and bring those dominators to their knees!
RobotsWin: Operation <clr>"Desert Disodane"<clrEnd> successfully completed. The Coalition Forces have won. <Player>, you showed your best!
Fragments of your offensive were aired by orbital satellites on the interplanetary news. You are our hero!
We expect you at the government building with a full report.

GovTextLoss: I admit, <Player>, the mission was too difficult and we should have waited for a more experienced ranger. However, what's done is done.
Despite your defeat, we'll be transferring a sum of <Money> cr to your account to cover the damages. That said, we will certainly try to make do without your services going forward.
GovTextStart: Would you like to take part in clearing out the Grand Canyon? It is an artificial island -- the dream of a loony millionaire, made real in the middle of an ocean. Ah, seems you've got a good nose for money, don't you? Don't look so surprised, we have devices that register greed.

Getting back to the matter at hand: after our system was liberated, we swiftly dealt with all the dominators on the planet and considered the matter closed. And then it turned out that this crazy millionaire had kept two samples for himself -- a blazeroid and a kelleroid. Evidently, he and his buddies thought to make a fortune on them. To this end, he built an entire base for the robots: a place to move about, engage in combat, etc.

We could go on with this fascinating story, but first we would like to secure your agreement, for if you aren't willing to help us, we will need to turn to another ranger. Well, what say you? Speak quickly! Will you save the Grand Canyon and fight the dominators on land? Or do you only fight them in space, aboard unbreachable cruisers?
02.GovTextWin: Dear <Player>, the Grand Canyon is quite an expensive piece of land. And your role in liberating this island is valued at <Money> cr, as converted to our tariffs. The money has already been transferred to your account!
02.Name: Grand Canyon
RobotsLoss: <Player>, you were defeated! Aye, life is full of sorrows. Word to the wise: stay away from these combat tactics in the future.
Prepare your report, as you well understand you won't be getting a standing ovation at the government building.
RobotsStart: Now that you have agreed to take on this mission, there is no turning back! Unless you mean to face trial by court-martial, that is. Forgive me, I got carried away; in fact, my objective is not to scare you but quite the opposite!

So, this millionaire guarded his subjects with a highly sophisticated security system, developed by Casperla Corporation. And yet, evidently, there is no such thing as a flawless security system. Something went wrong, the kelleroid hacked the system codes and went out of control. Within seconds of hacking the security system, the robot shut off all the electronic locks and escaped. They were about to go after him, but then it was discovered that the blazeroid was also at large. This red giant, however, wasn't going anywhere. He annihilated the millionaire and his subordinates, then started building fortifications that now span roughly 90% of the island's territory. Quite obviously with the intent of forming a landing party and taking over the whole planet!

The moment their distress signal was registered, military troops were dispatched on location. Our experts report that we still have one factory under our control in the Grand Canyon sector. Your immediate orders are to take over the factory. But your ultimate mission is to liberate the island! According to our data, kelleroids don't pose much of a threat, so destroying blazeroids should be your highest priority.
RobotsWin: Excellent, <Player>, our control over the Grand Canyon has been restored!
Strategists from across the globe followed your battles, and the vast majority were rather impressed with your tactics.
You have some time to rest before reporting to the government building.

GovTextLoss: Dear <Player>. You've failed our hopes. You should not have accepted this mission, for now the future of our planet's natural environment is a big fat question mark.

It goes without saying that we are not impressed with your work, and we will try to avoid doing business with you in the immediate future. However, as a civilized race it is our obligation to pay you an insurance premium of <Money> cr. A morale boost, if you will. Good luck.
GovTextStart: Yes, we have a mission for you, <Player>! Do you like nature? Trees, flowers, animals? If so, then you will surely be interested in this task.

A thousand years ago our planet was pure as a virgin spring. But as civilization grew and grew, we lost sight of our roots. Skyscrapers, factories and dump sites infested the planet. We didn't realize what we were doing to the planet's ecosystem, not until we were left with nothing...

Once we finally came to grips with this terrible fact, we proceeded to study the entire surface of our planet. Our search unearthed a tiny island, formed by a volcanic eruption many centuries ago and virtually untouched by civilization. Our scientists were delighted, for no alien flora and fauna could ever replace our own. According to our data, there is a small population of turtles on the island and some hundred species of plants, including the very last red flower, the name of which has been long forgotten. This island has become a symbol for us - a symbol that was modestly dubbed "Scarlet."

Now, I won't presume that you care about our flora and the dominators that threaten it. If that is the case, just say so. You are not a pirate, after all, but a true ranger, yes? Are you prepared to fight the dominators and save the nature of planet <Planet>?! If the answer is yes, we will deliver you straight onto the battlefield and give you all the necessary information about this noble mission.
03.GovTextWin: Congratulations on your victory, <Player>! Indeed, you are the savior of our civilization. We have planned the expansion of Scarlet Island for ten years ahead. Fundraising efforts are already underway, and seeing as preservation of nature is so costly, we apologize for only paying you this modest sum of <Money> cr.
03.Name: Scarlet Island
RobotsLoss: Argh, yet another failure!
No, you were not the first ranger who failed to deal with the dominators. We are expecting you with a full report.
RobotsStart: Excellent, <Player>, you are a true lover of nature for agreeing to take on such a difficult mission!

If you only knew how tenacious the dominators are in trying to break our will. They have visited our system numerous times, landing their troops here. We eliminated all their landing parties without mercy, that is until Scarlet Island came into the picture. This is not the case for heavy weaponry; nay, the job requires surgical precision. And that is exactly what we're tasking you with. You're not just some pirate, after all, we trust you fully.

As of today, the balance of forces on the island is pretty much equal. The detachment that you are taking over has factories, turrets and one robot-production facility. Along the warzone perimeter you'll find a variety of neutral buildings; they stand as a testament to the combat prowess of the rangers who came before you. We suggest that you capture them before the enemy does.

But don't lose sight of your main objective! You are there not to destroy soulless robots, but to save our natural environment. In light of this, please be careful and try not to use any heavy weaponry. Good luck in your cleansing efforts, <Player>!
RobotsWin: A fine victory, <Player>! We were right to have picked you for this mission. Scarlet Island is free!
Try to get some rest, and we'll see you at the government building. A special reception awaits you.

GovTextLoss: Alas, <Player>, your actions seemed to lack the ruthlessness so typical of the military. Now we will have to destroy the enemy labs from our orbit stations. It's a pity that we must lose such excellent research material on account of your failures.

Don't get antsy, we will still pay you a fee of <Money> cr for your efforts, inefficient as they were. After all, we promised you a generous reward, and faeyans always keep their word. But you mustn't expect to hear from us about any new missions any time soon.
GovTextStart: Yes, <Player>, we have a mission especially for you. We cannot entrust a matter of such importance to anyone else, for it concerns planet <Planet>, our home.

Many years ago, before the first faeyan colonists got here, this planet was inhabited by huge bugs. Yes, yes, these arthropods were sometimes the size of small towns! Unfortunately, we did not have a chance to study this curious phenomenon in detail, since the bugs died out aeons before we settled the planet. Anyway, it's not the bugs that are important here, but the dominators that started studying them. The robots grew intrigued by the extinct creatures' size and dropped a landing party onto our planet several months ago.
You are to stop their scientific efforts at any cost. You will receive detailed instructions once on location, and let me assure you that the fee will exceed any expectations you may have!
GovTextWin: Excellent! Thanks to your victory, <Player>, the kelleroids' research is ruined!
As thanks for your effort we have prepared a generous faeyan reward in the amount of <Money> cr.
04.Name: Bugs
RobotsLoss: Mission failed!
Ranger <Player>, abandon the battlefield immediately. You are expected to report to the government building.
RobotsStart: So, <Player>, as you might have guessed, this case is bug-related. Take a look at this map and note the landscape. It's obvious that one of those beasts died here some time ago.

Which brings us to your assignment. For purposes unknown to us, the kelleroids intend to study this fossil. Undetected by our radars, they landed right onto the remains of one of these insects and built a massive research base. In fact, we might not have even known about them if it wasn't for the blazeroid fleet that landed nearby.

Refusing to bow out, we went and built a base of our own, control over which is hereby entrusted to you, <Player>. Don't worry about the collateral damage, but stay focused on your target: the center of the island, where the kelleroids have dug a rather large hole. Whatever it is they're after, we want to study it too! We are the fae, after all!
Well, that's all there is! Now it's time for action!
RobotsWin: Excellent, <Player>, the remains are now completely at our disposal. We will surely find out what the kelleroids wanted here.
Hurry, a warm welcome awaits you at the government building.

GovTextLoss: Argh, <Player>! I always knew mongers like yourself could not be trusted with important missions.

If it were up to me, you'd get the death penalty for crimes far less serious than this, but, alas, the law is not on my side. Moreover, I must pay you a total of <Money> cr for your efforts to aid planet <Planet>. Now get out of my sight, I must find another ranger for this mission. And this time I am definitely hiring a maloq!
GovTextStart: We urgently need the help of an experienced strategist, <Player>!
Our planet has become an object of interest for the dominators due to its enormous mineral resources. Several months ago each robot type managed to land a self-extracting base here.

As the hostilities on the planet raged, the blazeroids and the terronoids pushed the kelleroids out of their main positions. Taking the opportunity, we dispatched a storm squad of elite maloq guards. A grand battle ensued, in which we seriously kicked the enemy's ass. And had it not been for considerable losses among our troops, we probably would have concluded the operation as planned.

As is, we need the help of an experienced ranger -- someone to utilize the resources at hand and recapture our main Agro-Intestinal refinery from the enemy. Being a trader yourself, we trust you understand how important this is to us? If you accept the mission, we will give you detailed instructions. And we'll surely make it worth your while. Even if you fail the mission, we promise not to execute!
GovTextWin: You did it, <Player>! You can always spot a true ranger.
We made the effort to contact the ranger center about your reward and were told that missions of this type are typically compensated in the amount of <Money> cr. We are glad to award you the money.
05.Name: Agro-Intestinal Refinery
RobotsLoss: Ranger <Player>. You were defeated. The agro-intestinal refinery is now under full control of the dominators.
Report back to the government building. I hope you have already taken the trouble to write a will?
RobotsStart: There, you have been delivered to the site of battle. The balance of forces on the territory of the agro-intestinal refinery is as follows:

You have one robot production facility and several resource extraction plants. That should be sufficient to show those tin cans what a true ranger is worth. The main danger you'll be facing are the terronoids; those vile green beasts literally swept through our old base. The kelleroids and the blazeroids are too preoccupied with fighting each other, so they are your secondary target.
Good luck, <Player>!
RobotsWin: Excellent work, Ranger <Player>, you've accomplished the mission! The agro-intestinal refinery is once again under our control.
The job was a doozy, so be sure to get some rest. You can reap the laurels of victory when you get your reward!

GovTextLoss: What a pity it is, <Player>, that the dominators have once again prevailed. Oh well, let them keep fighting one another. We will isolate this quadrant and grow twigs in the remaining one thousand three hundred twenty eight quadrants that are still under our control.

Clearly, entrusting this mission to a foreigner was a mistake. Rather than try to resolve the matter in a peaceful fashion, you rushed into battle without thinking twice. But it's no use talking about it now. May the omnipresent astral be with you; and with that, please accept this symbolic fee of <Money> cr. Though relations between us have certainly soured, tradition demands that we mustn't let a guest who tried to help to leave unrewarded.
GovTextStart: We have a mission for you, <Player>! Ever heard of something called the gaalian quadrants? No? They are traditional proving grounds, used by gaals to conduct large-scale simulations of real combat conditions.

The purpose of the dominators' last landing on our planet was apparently to undermine our military power by eliminating our combat proving ground. Of course, the very notion of "military power" is a slippery one, as for the past centuries we've dedicated ourselves solely to contemplation and enlightenment. The quadrant in question has long been redesigned to cultivate green twigs, and we are not presently capable of repelling the invaders.

There are virtually no brave youths among our people; your species, however, is renowned for producing many fine warriors. If you are one such warrior, <Player>, perhaps you might be interested in assuming temporary military command over the gaal armed forces on planet <Planet>? Truly, this is a rare opportunity for members of other races.
With your consent, our chopper will deliver you on location without delay; there you will receive all the instructions.
GovTextWin: We were informed that you weren't able to resolve this conflict in a peaceful manner. A pity, to be sure, but it takes nothing away from your accomplishment, <Player>. Indeed, today you have become a glorious part of gaalian quadrant history. My congratulations, and may the Astral be with you!

Our planet's economy is booming, and we can afford to be very generous with those who collaborate with us. As such, we have arranged for a round sum of 200,000 credits to be awarded to you for your efforts. However, supreme intellent has intervened and informed us that you do not engage in meditation during combat, which contradicts our postulate on the union of souls. Consequently, the money that was prepared for you has been reallocated to construct a monument to Makhpella, an unfortunate victim of the past war. Because the monument will be built exactly to scale, the project will require a whole lot of funding.
That said, we cannot let you go empty-handed. Please accept this modest fee of <Money> cr from the gaal twig-culturalist fund!
06.Name: Gaalian Quadrant
RobotsLoss: You lost the battle, <Player>. The quadrant remained under the robots' control.
Report back to the government building as soon as possible!
RobotsStart: Commanding Ranger <Player>, requesting permission to report:

The quadrant offers ideal battle conditions, having been designed by our top landscape engineers and preserved through the centuries. Enemy positions are essentially equivalent, though divided by water. For security reasons the quadrant was separated from the mainland by a wide stretch of water.

We do not consider violence to be the most efficient problem-solving method. It is always worth to try and resolve a conflict in a peaceful manner. Try to find a common language with the dominators, build yourself a robot, cross the river and establish personal contact. You have sufficient resources to keep your defenses for quite a while. Perhaps the dominators will agree to negotiate and will leave our planet voluntarily.
Remember that the Astral is always with you, <Player>. As such, the universe will never allow an act of injustice, no matter what you do!
RobotsWin: Did we... win? Were you truly able to solve this problem in a peaceful manner?! No? A pity.
Report to the government building without delay.

GovTextLoss: We had some time to analyze what has happened. Evidently, we gave you too few nuclear warheads; now we mean to make amends with this sum of <Money> cr for our lacking operational planning.

Let's hope that some other ranger will be able to finish what you started. In the meantime, our precious ragobam bullfrogs will have to learn to live in constant fear of explosions and war. Do you even understand how delicate their psyche is?! Emotional distress may cause them to fall into a stupor and stop producing their valuable resource! All in all, we are very disappointed, <Player>, and we think that you are partly to blame for this.
GovTextStart: We have a mission for someone who isn't afraid to get their hands dirty. A true master of their trade, a real pirate! By the way, I hope you harbor no perversions or unnatural inclinations for ragobam bullfrogs? Good, then listen carefully!

It is known that Ragobam Bullfrogs are a valuable source of the most delectable pleasure for Myriad clients. These wonderful creatures secrete a toxic substance that may induce intoxication, slight nausea and various psychosomatic effects, in addition to relaxation of cerebral lobes. Moreover, select gifted males may even even evoke visions of the future... They are an excellent commodity, popular even among Faeyans. Excuse me for getting carried away; you see, these Bullfrogs are my second biggest weakness. What is the biggest, you ask? That's privy only to my personal psychotherapist.

So anyway, we had this brilliant idea (we are a brilliant people, after all) to increase the population of gifted males! We imported dominators to our least profitable bullfrog farms, built up infrastructure and set up a base! You are given a huge resource and a whole lot of nuclear warheads to secure victory. And should the battle turn bloody, you will be rewarded in a way you've never even dreamed of. So, do we have a deal?
GovTextWin: You've done a great job radiating the territory, and we are utterly delighted by your actions. The bullfrog prides are mutating, the radiation is spreading quickly, and a good half of the population is totally high. We've even run into some difficulties. Over ten thousand pelengs were thrown in prison after attempting to get to your unforgettable island. Now all our youngsters dream about becoming ragobam bullfrog breeders, just like the glorious Ranger <Player>! They're even running away from home... What is the world coming to?! This is wonderful!

We trust you understand that our expenses for decontaminating the planet's territory have risen sharply. Though our budget has a huge hole in it, we ask that you still accept this modest reward of <Money> cr.
07.Name: Ragobam Bloodbath
RobotsLoss: Your defeat is like thunder on a clear day! Operation "Ragobam Bloodbath" is a complete failure! What are we going to do now? The area is badly irradiated, but the dominators are marching through our land!
Ranger <Player>, proceed to the government building immediately.
RobotsStart: Esteemed Commandant <Player>, we've decided to codename your operation "Ragobam Bloodbath"!

Your objective is twofold: try to make a whole lot of noise, and boost the radiation levels in the area to the max. Don't worry about the bullfrog farmers -- they are well familiar with the procedure and are safely hidden in underground shafts with enough supplies to last a hundred years. The main thing is keep the farm equipment intact and the larvae containers protected.

Now, let's get to it! The dominators are the real deal, and we honestly don't know what to expect. This is our first experiment, and we hope it doesn't get out of control. So, stay focused and alert. Let's rock!
RobotsWin: By Great Chvala! Operation "Ragobam Bloodbath" is a success! The bodies of the fallen dominators will soon host a fine brood of larvae!
<Player>, you have made excellent use of the resources provided. You have a couple of minutes to take a shower and report to the government building.

GovTextLoss: Ranger <Player>, you fought bravely, but the enemies were too strong. We truly believe that this defeat is no fault of yours; still, next time we would prefer to hire another ranger.
We wanted to send you on an all-expenses-paid vacation to our Jawaiian resorts, but for obvious reasons we will have to pay you the trip's monetary equivalent instead -- <Money> cr.
GovTextStart: We have a little mission for you. We're sure you've heard about our famous Jawaiian resorts? They are a chain of out-of-this-world-beautiful sandy islands. However, the islands were recently quarantined, and now all the tourists are sent to vacation at the famous Bloston Paradise orbital entertainment complex.

Naturally, the government ends up footing the bill, seeing as the tourism business is not the least bit profitable. And all because of the dominators! Some time ago those damned tin cans managed to secure a base in the Jawaiian Triangle and started up production of their own kind. Their attack claimed so many tourist lives that three of our insurance companies went bankrupt paying out premiums.

Now, I know that you're probably here for rest and not another fight, but put yourself in our shoes... Surely it won't trouble you much to organize resistance and drive the dominators out of our corner of paradise? For our part, we will provide you with everything you may need. If you agree to take over the planetary battle and win, our travel agencies will always be glad to treat you as an honorary guest!
GovTextWin: Ranger <Player>, you have saved us from bankruptcy. The Jawaiian resorts will soon reopen for business, though it can't happen soon enough! The orbital entertainment complex is about to collapse from the crazy torrent of tourists, and the tickets cost a small fortune!

We wanted to reward you with a VIP package to Bloston Paradise, but, sadly, the resort is fully booked 15 years ahead. This is why we're paying you a sum of <Money> cr -- the monetary equivalent of this upscale package. It's the next best thing to an actual vacation at Bloston Paradise!
08.Name: Jawaiian Islands
RobotsLoss: What a ferocious battle!

The situation appears to have gotten out of hand; we will need to refit the orbital entertainment center into a military cruiser and launch an offensive from outer space. What a shame that the Jawaiian Islands will be destroyed in the attack...
Please report to the government building.
RobotsStart: Thank you, <Player>, for agreeing to help us. I will see to it that you get the most accurate information on the subject.

The history of the Jawaiian Triangle goes back a long way; these sandy shores have been a favorite vacation spot among our people since... forever. Despite ample resources of ore, no one had ever even proposed extracting minerals here. But it seems that the dominators don't care for the sanctity of nature. They dug up the whole island, transforming gorgeous beaches into piles of rubble, then started burrowing deeper into the ground. Through it all, the dominator clans continued to war against one another; seizing the opportunity, we were able to snatch a corner of the triangle for ourselves.

But that was all we could do, and the dominators are fully resolved to restore the status quo. That is why we must ask for help. If you manage to secure this small scrap of land, you will have a shot at victory. This is a mission of the highest difficulty, so we won't hold it against you if you fail. Good luck!
RobotsWin: You've won, <Player>! Before long we will have everything back in order, and tourists will once again marvel in awe at our sandy shores!
We expect the victor to report to the government building.

GovTextLoss: Ranger <Player>, did you lose money on a race in the past and vowed to get us back or something? Your defeat seems awfully suspicious. Fess us now -- it was deliberate, wasn't it? Oh well, now we will need to take care of the dominators ourselves. Consider yourself lucky that we don't have any conclusive evidence, or else...

In any event, it looks like we will have to build a new track. My bosses have nonetheless decided to give you a small fee of <Money> cr, and I suggest you leave the money at the races, if they happen at all. Perhaps by immersing yourself in the exciting atmosphere of gambling and triumph, you will realize how you have robbed the fans of this sport.
GovTextStart: Oh, yes! Your timing couldn't be better -- the tournament is set to begin in two weeks! All the tickets were sold months in advance, and if the tournament falls through there will be a huge scandal...

Oh, you didn't know? ... You see, ours is the host planet for the annual ultraspeed foncer racing tournament. Unfortunately, ours is also the planet picked by the dominators as a target for sabotage! They captured a ship in the orbit that was transporting foncers for the tournament, and used them as a disguise to sneak through customs. Having infiltrated the island where the tournament is held, the dominators seized control and even built a few bases. And they did it right on the foncer speedway -- the Galaxy's one and only!

There's not enough time for us to build a new track before the tournament starts. That means you are our only hope, <Player>. If you purge the island of the dominator presence, we will have enough time to restore the damaged tracks and ensure the tournament takes place. If you only knew the magnitude and volume of bets placed, or the distinguished guests the tournament draws, you'd be ready to take on the dominators with your bare hands!
So, can you help us?
GovTextWin: Ranger <Player>, you are our savior. The tournament will take place, and I am confident that this year our ratings will go through the roof! And it's all thanks to the dominators!

First of all, our saga received tons of publicity across all media outlets. Even the military ones! A planetary invasion? We couldn't ask for more effective advertising! Second of all, we've decided not to restore the damaged speedway. Get ready, for this year the foncer tournament will be an obstacle race! The danger! The ambiance! Just imagine the track littered with still-smoldering dominator corpses and ruined bases...

The tournament committee has allocated a sum of <Money> cr for you out of the prize pool. The racers won't even notice it, but you have truly earned this money by risking your own life. Besides, you were something of an architect for the race track, hehe... Good luck!
09.Name: Foncers
RobotsLoss: Alas, <Player>, your titanic effort was not enough to secure victory.
Looks like the government will have to resort to other measures to resolve this matter.
Please proceed to the government building, you are expected.
RobotsStart: <Player>, you've come to our planet in a season of sweltering heat, which hopefully won't impair your command abilities.

Not long ago we captured a strategically important blazeroid base. The robots retaliated and tried to retake it, but we've been holding our own thus far. Most structures and dominator bases are situated along the track, making them easy to spot.
Your objective is to cleanse the island of excess junk. And by "junk" I mean dominators... Execute.
RobotsWin: Victory, <Player>!

The tournament will take place as scheduled. Should you decide to stay and watch the races, I recommend betting on Michael Schulmann. This hot shot has already won the race seven times, and remains in excellent shape!
Report to the government building for details.

GovTextLoss: Ranger <Player>, we thank you for your participation in this unique experiment.

Unfortunately for you, and much to the delight of revolutionary scientists, as we've dubbed the proponents of the intermittent intellectual development theory, their experimental model of the artificial pseudo-intellect <clr>Bambai-VI<clrEnd> proved to be rather efficient, since the dominators equipped with this "brain" pretty much wiped the floor with you.

The government will probably increase their funding, but something tells me that a portion of those funds will go toward neutralizing the insurgent machines. If you ask me, they should never have been programmed with personalities. By the way, this fee of <Money> cr is yours for participating in our scientific experiment.

But don't you dare blab about our research here, lest we declare you an industry spy and put a bounty on your head. We are rather disappointed with your intellectual capacity; in light of that, we're prepared to offer you a cerebral tissue transplant free of charge. This would allow you to use your brain with up to 70% more efficiency than other representatives of your race. Give it a thought.
GovTextStart: We believe that you will be able to help us correct the error made by the advocates of the revolutionary pseudo-intellect theory. This sorry bunch of dilettantes with the gall to call themselves "scientists" have begun a dangerous experiment on one of our industrial islands named Trilaran.

Not surprisingly, the experiment quickly got out of hand, as the advocates of the traditional evolutionary theory predicted all along. The experimental dominator models annihilated the Control and Surveillance sectors and are now wreaking havoc on the island unchecked. Thankfully, the would-be researchers failed to establish production of terronoids, and barely managed to activate their base.

We suggest that you make use of this base and its resources to destroy the sorry consequences of this experiment, and cleanse the island of Trilaran from the dominators. Obviously, we are not asking you to do this for free...
GovTextWin: Thank you, <Player>, the revolutionary scientists, as we've dubbed the proponents of the intermittent intellectual development theory, really owe you one! After all, it was you who cleaned up their mess...

As such, they have allocated a sum of <Money> cr for you as a token of their gratitude, though if you ask me, they could have been a bit more generous. Had it not been for you, the government would have pulled the funding for all of their upstart projects.

But hey, at least they've decided to name their new model of artificial pseudo-intellect after you: <Player><clr>-VII<clrEnd>. After all, you were the one to battle the dominators equipped with the <clr>Bambai-VI<clrEnd> series "brain" of faeyan production... But remember, this stays between us. We don't want some paranoid jackass to think we're producing dominators to enslave the other races, not while we're working for the good of the entire Galaxy!
10.Name: Trilaran
RobotsLoss: You lost, <Player>! This means that our experiment is over.
Your crushing defeat is proof positive that our innovations in the area of pseudo-intellect technology are a success.
As a direct participant of the experiment, you must report to the government building immediately.
RobotsStart: Commander <Player>, it is an honor to welcome you!

You will be taking control of an industrial base designed for terronoid study. Fortunately, it was never put it into operation. Now it's up to you to jumpstart the production of the combat machines, so let's not waste any time.

The island of Trilaran is shaped like a triangle, with all of its bases, including yours, situated in the corners. The center of the island is occupied by industrial complexes, which, according to the latest recon data, are yet to be discovered by the dominators.
I hope that this information will prove helpful, ranger. Good luck!
RobotsWin: Commander <Player>, you did it! The battle wasn't easy, but the joy of victory wipes away the weariness off our faces.
A government representative of planet <Planet> kindly requests that you visit him at his office.

GovTextLoss: Damn, <Player>! Now that's what I call talent! You looked like... well, like a boss! Thing is, you've got your nose too high up in the air, ranger. Don't deny it, how else do you explain deviating so much from the script? Have a look at the second to last page: "A complete and unconditional victory of the valorous Maloq Army..." Tell me, ranger, when did they start drafting dominators into the Maloq Army? Did I miss something?
You should thank our screenwriter... Against a background of smoking debris and jubilant dominators, he came up with a patriotic slogan that read:
"And where were YOU while you comrades were dying? Don't lose your chance to die a hero's death, join the valorous Maloq Army today!"
A real masterpiece, is it not? Ah, and here's your fee of <Money> cr. Finally, do yourself a favor and stay away from acting. It really isn't your thing, <Player>.
GovTextStart: "The valorous Maloq Army wants YOU!"
What do you say, <Player>, how is that for a slogan? I'm trying to write copy for a stereo trailer.

What for? Well, you see, our youth doesn't seem to want to serve in the army... But even the elite Red Army needs steady reinforcements. It's getting so bad they've started taking recruits with rosy and even pink mugs, instead of exclusively blood-red as stipulated by the Charter. If this keeps up, before long the Red Army will turn into an elite Rainbow Division. These damned kids have read too many adventure novels! Everybody wants to be a free ranger, but who's going to serve, I ask you? Division General Getraeus himself?
In an effort to boost patriotism among the youth, the brass has decided to shoot a promotional stereo trailer. We even got a cool script. Here, listen:

A ranger ship crashes on a dominator-controlled planet, right into a heated battle, where the valorous Maloq Army is giving the dominator forces a real drubbing, despite being greatly outnumbered. "Stop, where are you going?!" the ranger yells to the maloq troops fleeing in terror... I mean, regrouping! "Running to hide!"... Err, I mean... "We're falling back to lay an ambush!" the division commander fires back, and the next moment his head gets split open with a blaster. Blood is gushing, birds are singing, the grass is green and shiny... In a word -- beautiful! And then the ranger grabs hold of the banner, gives the troops a good kick in the ass... I mean, delivers a glorious and inspiring speech... and the galvanized maloq forces rip the dominators to shreds!

Then the ranger wipes the blood off his face and proudly proclaims: "I want to serve in the Maloq Army!" Cut scene. Say, do you want to play the part of the ranger, <Player>? The pay is pretty good. Everything is pretty much ready: a dominator party was delivered to the resort island where the filming will take place, and an elite storm squad is prepared to play the role of the maloq troops. Well, what do you say?
GovTextWin: A thousand supernovas, <Player>, didn't you read the script? It was a beautiful victory, to be sure, but the audience needs a dramatic ending... Your head was supposed to have been blown off...

How about a second take, eh, ranger? Actually, never mind, our filming budget is gone, and so are the dominators. We'll just need to add this frame with special effects. Obviously, we won't do it ourselves -- this kind of thing is beneath us maloqs. No, we've got a faeyan for situations such as this. He's got no legs but his hands are gold and his eye true. Oh, if only he had his legs, we would have turned him into a top notch sniper!
Anyway, here's your fee -- <Money> cr. The fees of fighters who had refused to take part in the filming were added as well, so the final sum turned out to be pretty decent.
11.Name: Maloq Movie
RobotsLoss: Cut! <Player>, what the hell?! Where is the triumphant victory over the enemy's superior numbers? Did you even bother to read the script, you space trash? Or did you swap scripts with the dominators?
Report to the government building at once!!!
RobotsStart: Commander <Player>, we've got a situation. Upon seeing how weak the dominator forces were, our elite troops ran off... I mean, refused to demean themselves by beating on such a helpless enemy.
In short, you will have to make do without them -- the trailer must be filmed at any cost. We've had to modify the script:

The crash-landed ranger finds an abandoned base and reactivates the production of combat robots. And then -- bang! -- the kelleroids come at him from the <clr>south<clrEnd>! Bang! -- now the blazeroids are marching from the <clr>east<clrEnd>! Long story short, the ranger takes a swig of alcohol, assumes the command, and wins the war. Wounded from the battle, he looks into the camera and whispers: "I want to serve in the Maloq Army!" -- and the next moment his head gets split open with a blaster. Blood is gushing, birds are singing, the grass is green and shiny... In a word -- beautiful!
In short, the spirit of patriotism of the maloq race is in your hands, <Player>. As for the dominators, it appears we have finally come to an agreement with them -- they are ready to advance.
Good luck, <Player>!
RobotsWin: Cut! <Player>, you are a superstar!!! Only pigheaded know-it-alls like yourself never seem to know how to follow instructions.
Just... report to the government building immediately.

GovTextLoss: Have some coffee, <Player>; and don't rush, you did everything possible.
You're probably not used to the local conditions: the cold, the snowstorms... And your sinuses can't be helping... Please, take my handkerchief.

On the plus side, now you know the quality of coffee at government institutions. I bet that's a check off your bucket list :-) We've transferred a total of <Money> cr to your account. Now rest up -- you've got lots more dominators to finish off and heroic feats to finish up. Though we hope you'll be continuing these efforts on other planets. Frankly, we're not especially confident in your abilities.
GovTextStart: We have a mission for you, <Player>, that is if you're prepared to brave the permafrost of our planet <Planet> a while longer.

Our scientists have recently discovered that blazeroid dominators are manufacturing their intellectual matrices in negative temperatures. This is why the robots tend to establish their manufacturing facilities on remote planets, where they engineer AI modules.

Our planet happens to offer ideal conditions for a production base, and blazeroids couldn't let the opportunity pass. To our shame, our planetary security systems missed their intrusion. However, we've managed to discover the dominators' landing point fairly quickly, and they have yet to secure a foothold on the island.

Furthermore, our saboteurs have captured one of the bases at the edge of the island. Alas, that is the only resource we can offer. Our planet is too insignificant to station regular forces, especially when they're needed elsewhere.

Finally, a small request: when you're killing robots, try to keep their frames intact as much as possible. Our planet is too poor in minerals to waste such ample amounts of top grade metal. You are a valiant warrior; no doubt, you realize how badly the Interstellar Coalition needs new battle cruisers.
GovTextWin: Ranger <Player>, we are happy to have selected you for this task. Even in the harsh conditions of permafrost, you've outdone yourself!

For a job well done, we hereby reward you with <Money> cr. Now, this sum isn't quite as big as you might like, but we did ask you to keep the robot frames intact. Instead, we've got an ocean of scrap metal to sift through! Having said that, we remain in utter awe of your courage and fighting ability.
12.Name: Permafrost
RobotsLoss: You've failed the mission, <Player>!
Maybe you should have worn an extra pair of wool socks. Sure, it probably wouldn't have helped you win, but at least your feet would stay warm!
Now take the nearest snowmobile to the government building.
RobotsStart: Commander <Player>, we're located at a base <clr>south<clrEnd> of the enemy position.

A power station is located somewhere in the center of the island. Its automatic defense system is sufficient to withstand the dominator attacks for some time, but if the robots manage to capture the station first, they will gain a huge advantage. Do not let this happen.
Unfortunately, the resources on this island are all tapped out, so you will have to make do with whatever reserve we have in stock, ranger.
Look alive, <Player>, or you'll freeze solid!
RobotsWin: You've won, <Player>!

Hard as it was, you gave those tin cans a good thrashing... A blow this hard won't be easy for the blazeroids to recover from -- just imagine how many robots have been stripped of their intellectual filling?
Head to the government building for your reward.

GovTextLoss: Frostbitten nose and glazed-over cheeks aside, you don't look half bad, <Player>!

Don't despair, for every failure is eventually followed by a victory. We even dispatched an elite squad codenamed "Frozen Seals" to assist you, but as soon as they learned they were going up against dominators, they, uh... disappeared. Not like you, ranger.
Your courage and goodwill have earned you this immodest gift of <Money> cr. Still, it's a pity we cannot trust you with missions of this magnitude.
GovTextStart: How is your frost resistance, <Player>? If all is well, then perhaps you can help us.

Some time ago we detected blazeroid and kelleroid landing parties on our planet's north pole. Given the extremely harsh conditions in the area, we weren't particularly alarmed by this news -- even machines cannot function well in such temperatures... Or so we thought, seeing as recently two fully functional bases were discovered in the area. Evidently, somehow the dominators managed to adapt.

We will provide you with experimental equipment, designed specifically for use in operations in subzero temperatures. Unfortunately, we never got the chance to test these new technologies, but our engineers swear that everything will work like clockwork in the far north... Let's just hope their idea of 'clock' is waterproof...
So, what is your decision, <Player>?
GovTextWin: Dear <Player>!

We've been glued to our screens, watching your feats with great admiration. Sure, there were a couple of anxious moments when we considered deploying an elite squad of mercenaries in snowshoes to your aid. They're codenamed "Frozen Seals" -- perhaps you've heard of them? Those boys sure charge an arm and a leg for their services... At any rate, we are happy to pay you <Money> cr in recognition of your services before our people. We trust this is a most wonderful reward!
13.Name: Heating Plant
RobotsLoss: You lost the battle, <Player>. Looks like our experimental tech was far from finished. The dominators are clearly superior to us technologically -- a lesson clearly demonstrated by your defeat.
We are expecting you at the government building.
RobotsStart: Commander <Player>, the base is entirely at your disposal. You mustn't tarry, but seize the initiative instead. You must turn the dominators into lifeless ice statues to serve as a vivid example for any other mechanical invaders that may follow.
Good luck! You're going to need it. And if you need reinforcements, let us know!
RobotsWin: Well, <Player>, somehow you've managed a mission that was truly impossible! What a glorious day for rangers everywhere!
Hurry now to the government building.

GovTextLoss: Achoo, <Player>! I mean, cheer up, <Player>. Guess this wasn't your day. And we had so much hope for you... No matter, our race can adapt to even the harshest conditions, though our survivability will really be put to the test now.

Go ahead and take a seat, ranger, if you're not afraid of having your posterior getting frozen stuck to the chair, that is, aaachoo! I hope you didn't catch a cold out there? There's something with your eyes, <Player>... Here, take this <Money> cr and run on over to the pharmacy for some medicine. And don't show your face around here again -- we've no need for losers.
GovTextStart: Aaachoo! Did you say something, ranger? If this is about coffee, I have bad news for you: all hot and alcoholic drinks -- achoooo! -- are deemed an important strategic resource here after the dominators pulled off a diversion on this planet just before it was liberated, cough-cough!

Wait, do you not know what's happening here? Then let me explain, cough-cough. But first, please turn up that heater... The dominators are still in control of our weather control station, which we have purchased from the fae for a hefty sum of money.

Running all the equipment chaotically like total idiots, they've managed to make the weather not only erratic, but simply deadly. Heavy snow in the midst of summer, devastating typhoons springing out of nowhere -- it's like we're in a disaster movie! We were hoping you could lead a rescue... a... a... aaachoooo!!! Pardon while I wipe that... operation? We must take back the weather station.
GovTextWin: Finally! <Player>, have you any idea what you've done for us? The death toll from the flu was beginning to look like a war report.

But now, thanks to you, everything should stabilize. Do you want my collection of warm clothes and blankets? No? Well, at the very least, please take this modest reward of <Money> cr? Come on, don't be shy, you deserve it!
14.Name: Weather Station
RobotsLoss: Now that's what I call a sneeze! And by that I mean defeat -- you don't often see this kind of fierce resistance even in human action movies about superheroes.
You fought nobly, but the conditions must have been a bit too harsh, to say the least?
Report back to the government building for a detailed debriefing.
RobotsStart: Commander <Player>, requesting permission to report on the current situation?
Reporting:

Aaachooo! There is a base <clr>southeast<clrEnd> of here that we've seized from the enemy, along with several production facilities. We didn't have enough time to launch a full-scale production of robots, but we did manage to store quite a bit of plasma for heating purposes. It is extremely cold down there, so I suggest that you always keep moving. Good luck, death to the dominators, and... achoo! Try not to get sick.
RobotsWin: A brilliant victory, commander <Player>!
You gave them a good drubbing, and I doubt the dominators are going to be back here any time soon.
Report back to the central government building to warm up and get some rest.

15.GovTextLoss: Your defeat indicates that the dominators are getting stronger. But that's not the bad news. The bad news is that you've failed to rescue the workers entrusted to you. I would gladly tear you apart, as I usually do with those who betray my homeland, the planet of <Planet>. Sadly, I cannot, 'cause we're under contract. I'm even forced to pay you <Money> cr for your "efforts"... But now I will ask you to go away. We need to plan a new rescue operation.
GovTextStart: Would you like some ice cubes, ranger? No? Too bad... Some smart ass -- some general's son, no doubt! -- has decided that our planet is an ideal place to mine ice. Now we're up to our ears in it... Many a maloq has already perished in the cold mines. We feel that it tempers the spirit and improves the nation's immune system.

But there was an unpleasant incident recently. Dominators have suddenly appeared in an open penitentiary camp -- a place you can't easily escape, obviously. As you would expect, the icecutters tried fighting them off with their bare hands. There were plenty veterans among them, but what's a pickaxe against a machine... You get the idea. They were brave, but they all died just the same... Argh... On your feet! Glory to the fallen heroes!

And now, let's get to it. Some of the inmates -- I mean workers -- escaped and hid in the barracks. They must be rescued before they freeze to death. Time is ticking -- there ain't no time to chillax! So, will you take on this rescue operation? Besides, some exposure to -40 temperature will be good for your pirate organism.
15.GovTextWin: Dear <Player>, you did it! You smashed those tin cans! We know that the cold helped you, 'cause nothing warms a warrior's soul better than overcoming hardships. But now you'll be looking to warm up with a drink, and we trust that a sum of <Money> cr will help. And don't worry about the icecutters -- they're doing what they love. This nation needs ecologically pure ice.
15.Name: Icecutting Inmates
15.RobotsLoss: Defeat, ranger... That's not how maloqs fight! Your mission is a failure, and the icecutters are dying in confinement because of you! Report to the government building immediately!
RobotsStart: Well, Ranger <Player>, now that you've agreed to the job offer, allow me to offer my condolences... We have only one factory and resources enough to build a handful of basic robots. You will need to act quickly and without error -- every minute counts.
If you let the dominators retake the initiative, they will show you no mercy. Good luck, you're going to need it.
RobotsWin: Victory! The great and mighty maloq word is victorious! The icecutters rescue operation will go down in history!
Report to the government building for a debriefing. I think there is a pleasant surprise waiting for you there.

GovTextLoss: Ranger <Player>, you've disappointed us. Now we'll need to blow up the entire lab, and because of you this whole island will sink underwater! We regret ever contracting you, as you are absolutely incompetent in this line of work. Please, just go.

Are you still here? What, you want money? After all that you've done for us? Fine, we'll pay you from our fund for the mentally retarded. It's got exactly <Money> cr. That will be sufficient, we trust? Now leave us...
GovTextStart: We have a top secret mission for you. I assume you know that our planet has just recently been liberated from the dominators. But only a few people know about the Time Laboratory. During their occupation of our system, the dominators were very much interested in it, so much so that it became a point of contention. In fact, even after being driven out of the system, they continue to remain there. The situation is fraught with all manner of disastrous consequences. What happens if the dominators go to the past and change it? The mere thought of it is truly terrifying!
Therefore, this mission will require an experienced strategist. Are you ready to turn back time, retaking control over the lab's surface and underground communication devices?
GovTextWin: <Player>, you cannot even imagine what the Time Laboratory means to us. It is more than just the property of our planet, but of the entire Interstellar Coalition. And all the credit in the world goes to you -- the ranger who gave us back hope!
From here on you may consider our world your own! And now, won't you please sign here in receipt of <Money> cr as compensation? We trust it will cover all your expenses.
16.Name: Time Laboratory
RobotsLoss: Mission failed! I fear this is the end for the Time Laboratory.
Sigh... All right, <Player>, report to the government building.
RobotsStart: Thanks for helping, <Player>! Let me give you the lowdown:

The lab has two main centers: Past and Future. The first has long been occupied by the kelleroids, while the second is in danger of being overtaken by terronoid squads. Thankfully, thus far they haven't been able to break through our automatic defenses. Blazeroid troops are making no efforts to get inside, as they are interested in the complex as a whole. But don't let the remote positions of the red robots fool you -- they are your most dangerous enemy!
We're giving you control of an excellent base, where we've already managed to build six combat units. Now it's your time to shine, ranger!
We all eagerly await your victorious return. Let time be on your side!
RobotsWin: A magnificent victory, <Player>! Time is now working for us!
Don't tarry in the lab, but hurry to the government building for a full operational debriefing.

17.GovTextStart: Map: Terron.cmap. Designed for the destruction of planet Terron.
17.Name: Terron
RobotsLoss: You've lost all the robots under your command. You mission to destroy Terron has failed.
<clr>Submodem<clrEnd> recommends that the user with the <Player> login leave this planet immediately.
RobotsStart: Two detachments of robots under our control are located in the vicinity of the Terron central processor, but the center is well protected from outside assault. The robots' combat protocol will not be able to overcome the enemy's superior numbers. You, Ranger <Player>, must take command over the robots into your own hands. The operation's probability of success equals 50%.

Using your main strike force, clear a path to the central processor. Locate the squad of robots armed with nuclear charges and activate them as close to the central processor as you can. This will initiate the irreversible process of disintegration of the entire planet.
<clr>Submodem<clrEnd> wishes you a good day.
RobotsWin: Attention! Danger! Disintegration initiated. You must leave this planet immediately.
<clr>Submodem<clrEnd> thanks the user with the <Player> login for shrewdly utilizing the resources at his disposal. End communication.

GovTextLoss: That was bad, ranger, very bad! It seems we cannot task you with missions of importance. Come back in a year and give it another go, if you want.
However, you were insured for the possibility of defeat, which means you'll be paid a sum of <Money> cr. Not bad for your first failure, eh, <Player>?
GovTextStart: And now it's time to practice. You have many battles ahead of you, but before you can take on serious missions you must first learn the basics of robot war tactics.

The first thing you need to learn that the best way to fight machines is with other machines. Our job in this equation is simple: controlling them. We will now give you a robot production facility. These machines are strong, but utterly without intellect. Our engineers have developed three basic programs for them: attack, capture and defend. Putting the robot into one of these three modes nets you an autonomous unit!

Of course, you don't actually have to use them. If you are a good strategist, you will be able to command your robots personally. Your objective is to force your way through the obstacles, destroy the enemy combat models and raze their base to the ground. We wish you luck. Remember that you're not actually in any danger. It's just training, <Player>, so be brave!
GovTextWin: Congratulations, <Player>! You've handled your first mission successfully.

We will inform the ranger center that you have completed your training, so that they can start recommending you as an experienced fighter. Your account is also credited with <Money> cr for completing the mission.
18.Name: Tutorial
RobotsLoss: Come on, <Player>. How could you possibly lose a practice battle?
Return to the government building with a report.
RobotsStart: I will be your instructor. I will teach you how to wage combat on the ground.

You are given a one robot production facility, which you can use to build a small robot army. The color of your robots is yellow. Enemy robots may be red, green or blue, reflecting the main colors of the dominator series.
There are training targets installed in front of your base. Before moving into action, take control of one of your robots to learn its movements and combat abilities.

Then move out and capture a couple of factories that yield resources for the enemy. This is not going to be easy! The robot models are designed for combat and will pose resistance. Eventually you will see the main enemy base. Once you crush their resistance, order your robots to capture it.
Now go, <Player>! And if you find yourself in a pickle, call for reinforcements and our helicopters will deliver our best robots to your aid!
RobotsWin: Well, the robots are history. Good job, <Player>!
Get some well-deserved rest, and report to the government building in the morning.

GovTextLoss: And there's our hero! Surprised? Don't be -- your reputation precedes you. And it is thanks to you that I am now at my post. And, naturally, everything will be very different now! I will cancel all educational programs, shut down free clinics, double taxes, and most importantly -- there won't be any feeding of maloqs to the sharks! It will be faeyans and piranhas instead!

Ha! A wonderful joke, was it not? You believed me, didn't you? And no wonder! If you didn't know, before becoming the Supreme Lyakusha I hosted a program called the Comedy Hour on a local stereovision channel. Anywho, it's time I assumed my new responsibilities. My first order of business will be related to the economy, namely lowering the fees or hired rangers by a magnitude of ten. Speaking of which, here is your rightly earned <Money> cr.
GovTextStart: <Player>! You should -- nay, you must! -- head to the Makhara-Tuta atoll at once! The atoll belongs to our Supreme Lyakusha, who loves to feed the sharks captive malo... I mean, captive macaques. Yes, of course I meant macaques!

But as ill luck would happen, as soon as our supreme leader arrived on his island with a fresh batch of captive ma... I mean, to engage in his favorite pastime, the island was overrun by dominators. Thankfully, our wise and handsome Lyakusha has managed to hole up in a bunker, which the dominators have already discovered and are trying to infiltrate as we speak!
We implore you to terminate the dominators and rescue our Supreme Lyakusha! He will make it worth your while and then some!
21.GovTextWin: You've saved our future! The thunderous applause in honor of your victory even caused a couple of columns in the government building to crack! But don't you worry, we've already deducted the repair costs from your fee. Now hurry and present yourself to your adoring fans! And don't forget your <Money> cr!
21.Name: Lyakusha's Residence
21.RobotsLoss: Brilliant! The enemy has penetrated the bunker, and I fear to imagine what they're doing to the former Supreme Lyakusha! You have executed our plan to terminate that fat sleazeball and sadist brilliantly! The entire peleng nation and captive maloqs are in your debt! Now head to the palace with your report, where our new ruler will personally shake your hand.
21.RobotsStart: The post of supreme commander is yours, ranger! We're pinning all our hopes on you, ranger! The entire population of our planet is counting on your villainy... I mean, on your valor and ability, seeing as the life of our beloved and most esteemed Supreme Lyakusha is at stake! Try to secure high ground at any cost and don't let dominators near that bunker!
21.RobotsWin: Brilliant! You've cleared the island, and the government starship is on its way to bring back the Supreme Lyakusha. You will have to make do with the regular military transport vessel, which will take you straight to the government building.

GovTextLoss: There he is! The party responsible for disrupting our planet's entire economic system, which is directly dependent on niobium export! Don't even bother with excuses -- it was your mission to keep the dominators from getting their hands on the niobium, but what were you up to instead?

Well, well... I think I know what you were up to... Our detectors show that you have 20 grams of niobium on you -- no more, no less! For shame, ranger! How dare you steal from your employer? This happens to be the last of the niobium left on our planet! You have a choice: either we declare you a criminal and execute you on the spot, or you immediately hand over the degradius skeletal fragment you stashed away so prudently?

Ha! Due to the critical shortage of niobium, its prices have skyrocketed, so I am now filthy rich! But don't worry, I won't leave you hanging either. Here, take this <Money> cr. And if that seems low to you, I'll remind you that I have you on video trying to steal this national treasure most shamelessly... You get my drift now, I trust? Best of luck now!
GovTextStart: We have a highly complicated but appropriately lucrative mission for you, <Player>!

Do you remember biology classes? Does the name "snoutius degradius" ring a bell? It is an incredibly rare species of giant reptiles whose skeletal remains develop deposits of the mineral niobium. And if you didn't know, niobium is the foundation upon which superconducting alloys are made. Ours happens to be the only planet that still contains live specimen of the giant degradius -- a fact that has catapulted our share on the galactic niobium market to nearly 28%!

Alas, all good things come to an end. The dominators have begun expressing strong interest in our source of niobium.  Having landed in a natural reserve, they butchered every single specimen of degradius in sight! They are now processing the poor creatures' remains, extracting niobium from their bones. You must put an end to this travesty! Exterminate every last one of the dominators and hand over the animal remains to our geneticists -- perhaps they will be able to clone them.
GovTextWin: Brave ranger! On behalf of our entire planet I wish to express our sincerest gratitude, and the material equivalent thereof in the form of this fee, totaling <Money> cr! So long now!

Freeze! Well, well... Our detectors show that you have 20 grams of niobium on you -- no more, no less! For shame, ranger! How dare you steal from your employer? I suppose I'd be willing to pretend to believe your story that this tiny bone simply stuck to the bottom of your shoe without you noticing, assuming you fail to notice me removing it and tucking it away in my pocket...
22.Name: Snoutius Degradius
22.RobotsLoss: How awful! While you were twiddling your thumbs and squandering our resources, not only did the dominators wipe the floor with you, they managed to load all the niobium onto their transport vessels and are about to leave our system! Report back to the government building at once!
22.RobotsStart: Welcome to the natural reserve of the degradius -- the Galaxy's number one endangered speci... Oh, who am I kidding -- this one-of-a-kind creature is pretty much extinct. Your objective is simple -- to stop the dominators. Not a single gram of niobium must leave this planet!
22.RobotsWin: Good job! The scientists are setting up their equipment as we speak. Let's hope we can use those gaalian technologies to clone the degradius. It's too bad we didn't think of it sooner! You may return to the government building now.

GovTextLoss: Seriously, <Player>?! It takes talent to be as bad as you are in battle. Evidently, we'll need to approach a more experienced commander and try to mount another offensive. Look, we know you tried your best, so you can have your compensation of <Money> cr. The money has been transferred to your account.
Goodbye!
23.GovTextStart: <Player>, we need you to spearhead the liberation of the Grand Crater island. Besides its unique shape, resembling a parabolic dish, the island is particularly rich in chrysolithe deposits. We suspect that the terronoids aim to use the chrysolithe as foundation for a massive hyperspace radar. And you can bet that this communication facility will be used against the Coalition. Your mission is to recapture the bases and factories, and sweep the area clear of enemies. The operation might be further complicated by the fact that two detachments of hostile robots have been spotted moving toward the island.
GovTextWin: Our congratulations, <Player>! The captured radar was in perfect order, meaning we can use it to pick up the weakest of signals from even the most remote star systems... For instance, we've just caught the Howard Cistern show on an Earth radio station. And the reception is pretty darn good! We shudder to imagine the role this device could have played in the metallic hands of the invaders.
Your fee of <Money> cr has already been transferred to your account. Be well!
23.Name: Antenna
RobotsLoss: You lost the battle, <Player>! How could you let that happen?! The odds were on our side, but you blew it... Argh!
Report back to the government building at once, <Player>! We're expecting you.
23.RobotsStart: Our intelligence reports were confirmed. The situation on the island is trickier than we initially thought, as kelleroid and blazeroid detachments have invaded reinforced terronoid positions. You need to act quickly and capture the bridgehead while the "hosts" are dealing with the competition. Your main objective is to destroy all hostile robots and establish total control of the gigantic island slash radar, breaking off all contact between the broken dominator forces and their main host in the other star systems.
23.RobotsWin: You did it! I can hardly believe what I'm seeing on the monitors! That was glorious, <Player>! Hurry over to the party hall in our planet's government building!

GovTextLoss: Alas... You've failed the mission, and we were forced to sink Endoria's Pride. The fact that the invaders perished along with the ship is little consolation, considering that this war has claimed all three of our floating research and development centers. Our planet's economy is now in serious peril, for we are no longer capable of providing for our most basic needs.
I guess this <Money> cr belongs to you. I wish I knew why you're being paid at all, having failed the mission so spectacularly, but our government transferred the money to your account just the same.
GovTextStart: How do you feel about walks on the beach, ranger? Fresh salty breeze, water splashing your face, the smoking remains of enemy ships and the floating bodies being devoured by sharks... Oh, apologies, I got carried away.

This morning we picked up a signal from a floating research and development center, located aboard the ship Endoria's Pride. The ship was attacked by dominator vessels, likely intrigued by the complex's powerful manufacturing bases and research labs.
If you head over to Endoria's Pride and help us defend the ship against the dominator offensive, you will earn a sizable reward if the operation proves successful.
GovTextWin: You did it! Had the dominators been allowed to capture the complex aboard the vessel, we would have no choice left but to sink Endoria's Pride! Over these years of fighting the dominators we've already lost two similar ships, crippling our manufacturing capacity.
As a token of our gratitude, please accept this modest fee... Check that, let's call a spade a spade -- this fee of <Money> cr is pretty darn impressive!
24.Name: Landing
24.RobotsLoss: <Player>, evacuate immediately! The vessel is about to be take over by dominators. The moment that happens, we're going to sink the ship to keep it from falling into enemy hands. Now hurry!
RobotsStart: Aha! You must be the ranger that the brass told us about? The one who's going to take command of this defense operation? Great, you're finally here. The dominators are pushing from all sides, and we're barely holding them back.
Our manufacturing centers are working at full capacity, churning out combat technology. Those microprocessor-powered tin cans will be sorry they ever attacked us!
24.RobotsWin: Excellent job! The dominators have been repulsed, and our technicians were able to patch up their ships, giving us the chance to research dominator technologies. You're expected at the government building with a report, so hurry!

25.GovTextLoss: Thanks to your dreadful leadership, <Player>, this area of the Placid Ocean will remain perilous for seafaring. We hope you take the time to reconsider your choice of careers. Rather than commit more epic fails such as this, you might be better off sitting in a bar somewhere, getting tanked and bragging about your would-be victories to other losers like you. We'll even pay you this <Money> cr to get a headstart on it.
25.GovTextStart: <Player>, this should be a straightforward operation to capture a metal processing plant. Squads of blazeroids and kelleroids have secured a foothold inside it. The plant is stationed in the middle of the Placid Ocean, which creates a hazard for passenger vessels with routes in the immediate vicinity. We trust it won't be too difficult to lead a landing party of robots to victory and liberate the island?
25.GovTextWin: We're mighty grateful, <Player>! Not only did you decimate a bunch of pesky machines, you've also ensured safe passage for ships in this sector of the Placid Ocean here on planet <Planet>. As such, this sum of <Money> cr is yours by right.
25.Name: Iron Island
25.RobotsLoss: You lost the battle, <Player>! And in so doing you missed the perfect opportunity to drive the dominators from the island. Proceed to the government building immediately.
25.RobotsStart: Your timing couldn't be better! Your detachment of combat machines has just landed on the plant's helipad. It's your time to shine, <Player>! Oh, yes... Our hackers have a pleasant surprise for you: they were able to temporarily cut off the dominators' control over two of the bases. You mustn't miss this opportunity!
25.RobotsWin: Now that's what I call a brilliant victory! You handled that better than we could ever hope for, <Player>! Hurry back to the government building for your reward.

26.GovTextLoss: It really is too bad that you weren't able to liberate the island, <Player>. The only thing we can do now is hope the Warden's strength will prevail, and that we'll get luckier in our choice of a commander in the future. May Aabyr-Vaalg be with you, and here's your compensation for any suffered stress in the amount of <Money> cr.
GovTextStart: According to your dossier, <Player>, you are a seasoned commander of ground robot forces. As such, we've decided to entrust you with the honorable mission of liberating Pyramid Island -- a truly unique site serving as evidence of an ancient civilization on planet <Planet>. We know next to nothing about this culture, for they've disappeared from here long before we settled these fertile lands. That is what makes the recovery of the island so critical for our scientists. Without it, they will not be able to study the remains of this extinct nation.

A squad of robots under your command will be delivered to the dome of the main pyramid. From there, it's your time to shine. Are you ready to liberate this precious architectural ensemble from the dominators? We will do all that we can to assist!
26.GovTextWin: May the power of the <Star> shine upon you, <Player>! You are a true warrior, and we vow to engrave your name on the granite Slabs of Glory, sacred to planet <Planet>. But for now, we humbly ask that you accept this fee of <Money> cr.
26.Name: Pyramids
26.RobotsLoss: Defeat! Seriously, again?! Err... You see, you're not the first contractor we've deployed to this island... And not the first to fail, obviously. No matter, we will keep trying again and again.
26.RobotsStart: Hrm. We're sorry, <Player> -- our pilots had a poor grasp of the Pyramid Island geography, so they ended up delivering some of the landing party to the smaller pyramid instead of the the main one. Also... The blazeroid presence on the island was terrifying! Half an hour before your landing, our scouts reported that the sculpture of the Guardian, once deemed a purely decorative element of the ensemble by our scientists with its face always turned to the <Star> star, had "come alive" and begun to destroy all resource-gathering constructions! What is more, the dominators seemed utterly powerless to stop it! To their credit, the machines quickly recovered and deactivated the remaining bases, meaning you will also need to rely on the existing stock of resources. As soon as production halted, the Warden froze still, no longer reacting, not even to blazeroid attacks. The dominators picked up on that as well, and are now amassing a massive army for a decisive attack on the island's Guardian. Don't let them destroy this magnificent creation of an ancient and clearly wise civilization!
26.RobotsWin: That was just... brilliant! You've handled the resource deficit problem with enviable skill. Hurry back to the government building and share with them the wonderful news of the Pyramid Island's liberation!

GovTextLoss: How terrible, ranger! Look at this satellite recording, which captured the final moments of the Meridian Border before it was dispatched by the dominators to kingdom come! And if that's not enough to make you cower in shame, the geographical society has allocated a sum of <Money> cr to help awaken your conscience.

By the way, our orbital observation crews have recently spotted a dominator satellite spy floating directly over the island that has what our geographers call the Equator. That is yet another of our planet's attractions. But this time around we prefer to act without your "assistance."
GovTextStart: If you've ever been to our planet before, surely you've heard of the Meridian Border, yes? No?? How strange... All right, I'll give you brief background info. A thousand years ago a symbolic boundary was set on one of the islands in the ocean, splitting our planet into western and eastern hemispheres. All the geography maps produced since have been created with prime meridian tracing this line with utter precision, making it one of our planet's essential symbols!

But recently the island containing the meridian boundary was captured by the dominators. They razed the local tourist town to the ground. We were lucky that this isn't tourist season -- the island was closed to visitors, so there weren't any casualties... Of course, that doesn't mean we should sit idly by and watch the dominators destroy the Meridian Border with their stations! The planet's geographical society has allocated a sizable donation to whoever can thwart the dominators' plans! And you have all the chances of earning it if you accept this mission.
GovTextWin: Excellent job, ranger! Good work calls for a suitable reward, so please accept this sum of <Money> cr -- you've earned it! By the way, our orbital observation crews have recently spotted a dominator satellite spy floating directly over the island that has what our geographers call the Equator. That is yet another of our planet's attractions. So keep your communications line open -- we may have need of you again.
Best of luck, ranger!
27.Name: Border
27.RobotsLoss: You didn't make it! Of course, we'll drive the dominators from the island sooner or later, but I fear it will be too late for our precious Border. By then it will have been destroyed, and we will need to create it anew. As for you... please report to the government building.
RobotsStart: Greetings, ranger! The geographical society will supply you with their proprietary research and development centers, used to manufacture super-accurate measuring equipment to analyze the impact of atmospheric and tectonic processes on the terrain relief... It shouldn't be difficult to reconfigure the machines to start producing modern combat technologies instead -- no worse than those wielded by the enemy. The required programs have been received and integrated.
The dominators settled on the peak of a mountain ridge, which is also where the Border lies -- a gorge stretching strictly from north to south and dividing the ridge in two.

After observing the dominators carefully, our specialists noticed a curious fact: it seems that the dominators on the western ridge dislike their eastern brethren.
