The enmity appears to be mutual, and if it wasn't for the Border, the two factions would have wiped each other out by now. Unfortunately, that doesn't make your job any easier, as the enemy's positions are much too strong to attack them head-on. No, the situation calls for more brains than brawn. Anyway, good luck!
27.RobotsWin: You did it! And just in time, thankfully -- the Border is still intact. You are expected at the government building with a report.

28.GovTextLoss: Do you hear that, ranger? The roar of the crowd outside the government building? That's our entire Scientific Academy, demanding as one that you be handed over to them, to be torn limb from limb. We've been waiting for years for an opportunity like this -- to get our hands on an intact dominator ship. Count your lucky stars that we're a civilized planet; otherwise you'd be facing certain and very painful death at the hands of rabid professors and academics. Here's your <Money> cr. I suggest you change your appearance and leave this planet as soon as possible.
28.GovTextStart: <Player>, recently we have come upon a drifting kelleroid Equantor way out in far space. It has sustained significant damage and could easily be destroyed, but that's not what we want. Rather, we want to take advantage of this golden opportunity to capture and study it thoroughly. Our plan is to furtively deploy a squad of reprogrammed robots and have them make the capture. We already have a key for the gate.
28.GovTextWin: We were right to choose you to perform this mission, <Player> -- you were simply brilliant! Of course, the robots you commanded roughed up this invaluable device quite a bit, and we were even considering deducting 50% from your fee, but our scientists claim that no critical elements were damaged. Therefore, you can thank our eggheads for getting paid the full <Money> cr. And now, here is your money, as agreed.
28.Name: Equantor
28.RobotsLoss: How awful! Admittedly, we knew that this venture was a long shot, but your handling of the situation was so utterly inept that I'm ready to strangle you with my bare hands, <Player>! Do you even realize what this opportunity meant for us? Now get out of my sight! I hope our government will punish your incompetence accordingly.
28.RobotsStart: You will have only two robots under your command; our analysts fear that a higher number of infiltrators might activate the ship's self-destruction mechanism. Let's hope they won't be met with heavy resistance. According to scouting reports, the crew of Equantor are busy repairing the ship, namely the engines and the central computer. This should keep the metallic beasts from putting up a coordinated defense, giving us a certain advantage.
28.RobotsWin: Brilliant work, <Player>! I bet your scientists will enjoy rummaging though the innards of the ship you've captured. I for one can hardly wait to read their reports! Now hurry over to the government building for a debriefing.

GovTextLoss: Looks like you've doomed our entire planet to certain death. The earthquake zone has already doubled and is continuing to expand. We've already declared a state of emergency and commenced with evacuations of the population.
I suppose you're still due this fee of <Money> cr for trying and getting your hands dirty. We cannot afford to pay more -- the rest of the funds will be used to evacuate our people.
GovTextStart: After the Coalition forces drove the dominators from our system, we spotted a disguised enemy transport vessel and shot it down. It crashed on one of the islands in the ocean and by some miracle didn't explode or even catch fire; it stands to reason that the cargo it was carrying is still intact.

We suspect that this cargo is some kind of matter distorter. Not only did the device survive, but it appears to be in perfect working condition, judging by the slew of earthquakes that keep rocking the area within a 1,000 km radius of the crash site.

Our technicians should be able to switch off the device, but a dominator force has already landed on the island and is attempting to recover the lost cargo. Your job is to clear the area of dominators, allowing our scientists to first deactivate the module and then to study its mechanisms.
GovTextWin: I'm glad to see you justify our confidence in you. Our scientists are already hard at work over the device, having thoroughly studied more than 80% of the mechanisms. Suffice it to say that results have been impressive! For example, they have yet to discover even a single element unknown to Coalition scientists. It wouldn't surprise me to learn that the device was captured by the dominators on one of our own planets, and that all those earthquakes were a mere coincidence. Then again, it must hold some value -- why else would they have fought so fiercely to get it back?
Anyway, this <Money> cr is yours by right for completing the terms of the mission.
29.Name: Module
29.RobotsLoss: Hmmmm.... Either all my monitors are out of order, or you've suffered complete defeat and lost all the bases and robots? If it's the latter, fall back immediately and report to the government building at once.
RobotsStart: Well, <Player>, you're on location.

The fallen device comes with an autonomous security system which destroys any creature that comes near it, including dominators. The jacket of this module protects the security controls, and it's unlikely that the surface robots' weaponry can damage it. The dominators have erected four aggregates at the crash site that are supposed to deactivate the defense and switch it over to a friend-or-foe mode. Currently they are fighting for these four key points, each of which is responsible for a certain component of the security system.

Your mission is to take control over all four points and deal with the dominators, whereupon our scientists will take care of the module. To this end we have set up a production base for you, and the dominators know nothing about your imminent engagement. Good luck!
29.RobotsWin: Magnificent! You've done your part brilliantly, and now it's up to our technicians to do theirs. You can go back now...

GovTextLoss: Well, Ranger <Player>.

Firstly, thanks to your incompetence we have lost a super-modern research complex, along with a whole series of experimental aircraft. Secondly, we know how rangers like gossiping with their buddies over a glass of tokilla. As such, we're entirely certain that the secret of the island will remain a secret.

The smart solution would be simply to execute you. As a spy, a saboteur... And to relieve some stress. Alas, such methods are unbecoming of our people, so take your <Money> cr aka hush money and get out of here before we change our mind!
GovTextStart: Well, Ranger <Player>, it just so happens we're in need of a seasoned strategist, and I do hope you fit the bill.

Your mission will be to retake the Isla-Mayolina Island back from the dominators. Perhaps you've heard something about this barren and utterly useless piece of rock? If you have, congratulations -- you've fallen for our misinformation campaign. The fact is that we've been deliberately trying to keep this place out of the public eye, going as far as staging phony shows and anti-promotional events. The truth is that the island is used as a testing ground for our latest top-secret technology – unmanned stealth aircraft. Unfortunately for us, the dominators don't seem to care much for our evening news programs. Knowing not the uselessness of the island, they up and captured it for themselves.

So, are you willing to help us drive the dominators from the island and return this utterly worthless piece of work to the authorities of planet <Planet>? Naturally, your service will be subject to renumeration, specifically 1,000,000 cr! An unbelievable sum, is it not?
GovTextWin: Brilliant, magnificent, spectacular, Ranger <Player>!

The security cameras mounted on the stealth aircraft broadcasted a life feed of the entire operation, finally proving beyond a shadow of a doubt that there is absolutely nothing of interest on this island. Especially now that half the aircraft were destroyed by your overzealous robots! Of course you didn't notice -- they were stealth aircraft, after all!

Now... Accounting for damages suffered in the form of the destroyed aircraft, the environment tax levied for releasing so many toxic fumes into our planet's atmosphere, as well as a compulsory contribution to the Klissan War Veterans Fund, please accept the remainder of your fee -- <Money> cr. Don't even try to refuse our generosity -- we'll have none of that now! And don't forget that the Isla-Mayolina Island is hands down the most wretched and unremarkable place on this planet. I trust we understand each other?
30.Name: Isla-Mayolina
RobotsLoss: Well, well, Ranger <Player>!
Honestly, I expected more from you.

You've ruined all our plans and hopes! Maybe you're an enemy spy and were working for the dominators all along? I suspect you'll be hearing from our counter-intelligence service soon enough. They won't shoot you, but you can probably look forward to spending the next 300 years in a dark cell!
RobotsStart: Thank you for agreeing to help, Ranger <Player>! Our situation on the ground isn't great -- we were able to put a landing party in the south and build a fairly protected base, but then the entire party was destroyed while on a scouting run. The base and all its resources, however, are yours to control, ranger.

A detachment of kelleroids has dug in to the northwest, and in the east you'll find an entrenchment of terronoids. And if that scenario seemed too easy for you, our satellites have just spotted a blazeroid party landing in the southwestern part of the island. This is a pickle, to be sure, but it could be used to our advantage if you manage to get the dominators fighting amongst themselves.
Try to find and capture production complexes designed to test the effectiveness of aircraft against ground targets -- those should still be functional. Good luck!
RobotsWin: Excellent work, <Player>!

We were finally able to force the dominators off this lifeless and utterly unremarkable island. I still can't believe that before you came along we've already managed to flush nearly half of the planet's budget down the toilet!

GovTextLoss: A-a-a! There he... hic!... comes... Yes, yes, I've heard that the island has been liberated. Don't just stand there -- pour! What do you mean, you don't drink while on duty? You're working for me, and I say you can drink!

The worst thing about it, ranger, is that I was willing to do anything for her! The ring, the island... I was even practicing calling my would-be witch of a mother-in-law "mom"... All the while she's been cheating on me with some rotten flight attendant! So tell me, what does that make her? And what does it make me? And why are all women such... such... such women?! She was my everything...

Who's there? Oh, it's you, ranger. What do you need? Money? But you didn't earn it! Tell me, ranger, do you think I'm funny? Funny like I'm a clown? No? Well, then here's your <Money> cr. Go to a bar and drink to my health, eh...
GovTextStart: I have an offer for you that's rather personal in nature. But I'll make it worth your while if you help me -- this I promise you. You see, I've been dating my girlfriend for quite a long time now. I love her and I've finally decided to propose, and I'm certain that she'll say yes. And why wouldn't she? Do you know a girl who would refuse a 50 carat black diamond ring and her own personal island?!

My analytical adviser devised a grand and super-romantic plan: I hand my beloved the ring when we're on the orbit, aboard my luxurious space yacht, then point to the heart-shaped island in the window and say: "My darling. There is my heart, and now it belongs to you!"

Very romantic, isn't it? It took me three hours to memorize the line! Or rather practicing it in front of a mirror. But alas... Turns out the island I'd bought has a dominator base on the surface, which I suppose explains the 30% discount! Quite a present it would make, eh? <Player>, if you help cleanse my heart... meaning this island of the dominators, you will be generously rewarded!
GovTextWin: A-a-a! There he... hic!... comes... Yes, yes, I've heard that the island has been liberated. Don't just stand there -- pour! What do you mean, you don't drink while on duty? You're working for me, and I say you can drink!

The worst thing about it, ranger, is that I was willing to do anything for her! The ring, the island... I was even practicing calling my would-be witch of a mother-in-law "mom"... All the while she's been cheating on me with some rotten flight attendant! So tell me, what does that make her? And what does it make me? And why are all women such... such... such women?! She was my everything...

Who's there? Oh, it's you, ranger. What do you need? Money? Here you go... I sold the ring and the space yacht, and I'll sell the island as well... And I'll invest it all in alcohol production. Take this <Money> cr. That should cover it. By the way, you want to partner up with me? Ohh, my bitter, biiiitter faaaate...
I don't waaaanna be druuuunk on wiiiine... I waaaanna be druuuunk on your loooove...
31.Name: St. Valentine's Island
31.RobotsLoss: Damn it, ranger! I regret letting my crew get some rest -- I just knew you'd botch this up! Neither your nor my employer will be happy about this. Good luck, and I hope your employer won't be too pissed... Considering the upcoming wedding! Please pass along my and my boss' warmest regards for the newlyweds!
RobotsStart: Greetings, ranger! The island's former owner was highly distressed to learn the true identity of the bigwig he had slipped this dominator-infested rock to. Naturally, there won't be any refunds given, but he did send me to help you resolve this rather unpleasant development.

My crew and I have already roughed up the dominators some and even captured some of their structures. Now we're off to the repair base, leaving you to finish what we've started. And if things get hairy, give us a ring and we'll try to help.
Talk later!
RobotsWin: Excellent job! You were able to drive the dominators from the island. Please send my boss' warmest regards to your employer! I trust that the two parties can put this misunderstanding behind them, considering all's well that ends well?
Please pass along my and my boss' warmest regards for the newlyweds!

GovTextLoss: Watch it! Don't come any closer! Sure, my radiation meter is quiet, but what if it's broken? Alas, it looks like we've lost the sanctuary. Our biosensors don't detect a single living soul on the island, save for the dominators. Of course, some of the mutants down there weren't always detected by biosensors...

If you ask me, you should be thrown out of here without pay. Unfortunately, the law dictates that visiting a contaminated zone means we must allocate this small sum of <Money> cr for your treatment, lest you start looking like our dearly departed specimens!
Now take your money and go!
GovTextStart: We've... We've got a suitable mission for you, he-he! And it happens to be in the largest cultural center of our planet, so count your lucky stars!

Does the name Black Bill Atoll mean anything to you? It's clear now that you have absolutely no knowledge of interplanetary tourism! It is a giant museum island, featuring some of the Galaxy's most spectacular creatures whose very appearance rocks your imagination! At least that was the case before dominators landed on the island and took it over! I fear they've already exterminated the most valuable specimens... You're the only one who can stop them from turning our tourist paradise into a barren, radioactive wasteland...
GovTextWin: Watch it! Don't come any closer! Sure, my radiation meter is quiet, but what if it's broken? By the way, not only did you successfully defend our sanctuary against the dominators, you've managed to significantly increase the island's radiation levels! Mutants have been popping up like mushrooms... And you should see what actual mushrooms mutated into! Then again, you shouldn't -- not if you value your sleep.
Anyway, we've decided to throw in a bonus in addition to your fee, so here's <Money> cr.
Make sure to drop by our mutant sanctuary when you get the chance -- you're going to love it!
32.Name: Atoll
32.RobotsLoss: Gah... Unsurprisingly, you really screwed that one up, ranger. The dominators made mighty quick work of you. All the better, I suppose. If you had lingered longer, you probably would have grown a tentacle or an extra pair of eyes on your back. Then again, a mutant ranger would have been quite the hit!
RobotsStart: Welcome to Black Bill Atoll, the largest uranium-235 deposit on planet <Planet>! No, no, you heard me right -- this island is literally blazing radiation. But the government didn't lie to you -- it really is a tourist attraction. Only it's not a zoo with rare animals, but a real-life mutant sanctuary! Watch, even the soles of your boots will soon be mutating before your very eyes, he-he.

You see, showing these mutants to tourists is far more lucrative than mining all this uranium. But unless you kick the dominators from the sanctuary, this populated radioactive wasteland will soon become barren. Unless you suggest we fly in tourists to gaze at the dominators! Best of luck, ranger. But make sure you don't linger here... Unless you want to join this menagerie, he-he!
RobotsWin: Good job! I didn't expect you to be done so soon. I bet you were expecting to grow a tentacle or change skin color at any moment, am I right? You shouldn't worry so much -- we would have found work for you easily... As one of our dearest specimens, of course. A mutant ranger would have been quite the hit!
Fine, fine, I'll stop. Please return to the government building.

GovTextLoss: Ranger, do you realize what you've done? Now we have no choice but to carpet bomb the entire pyramid complex... Or, what's worse, to deploy a landing party of maloq mercenaries on location... Those boys are like gobsauri in a china shop -- we won't find a single stone to study once they're finished, never mind a pyramid! So I suggest you leave now...
Oh, hold on a minute. I completely forgot that you're still due a minimum of <Money> cr for taking part in the combat operation. And now -- out of my sight!!!
GovTextStart: Ranger <Player>, you are quite the experienced commander. How would you like to serve the cause of science in exchange for some large reward?

Perhaps you've heard about an ancient interplanetary civilization whose remains have been found on dozens of planets? Most often these were constructions of pyramids. Case in point, a whole complex of excellently preserved pyramids has been discovered on the unpopulated hemisphere of our planet. But what's really interesting is the fact that the island had become visible only recently. Until then, it somehow eluded all our detectors. Our theory is that an ancient cloaking device had finally malfunctioned...

Sadly, upon deploying an expedition to the pyramids, we discovered a detachment of kelleroids on the island! They were digging shafts into the island depths; according to our data, that is where the pyramids connect via a network of tunnels and corridors. Fortunately, the expedition was carrying enough tech and weapons to capture one of the dominator bases up in the mountains. And that's where we stand now -- in dire need of a professional dominator fighter. Help us liberate the island from those grabby manipulators. The pyramids must be handed over to our scientists for study!
GovTextWin: We were right to trust you, <Player>!

Our scientists are already hard at work, and the early results are quite promising. In no small part thanks to kelleroids, incidentally, who have left behind all kinds of computer files in the mainframe. But I won't bore you with the details. Instead, I will gladly award you this reward of <Money> cr from the Science Fund of planet <ToPlanet>. I hope that this money will help you in the war against the dominators.
33.Name: Trident
RobotsLoss: Oh, <Player>!
I don't believe my eyes! You've lost our last base, stripping us of all hope of studying the pyramids on this planet. Report back to the government building at once.
33.RobotsStart: Ah, there you are, ranger! The kelleroids have been pretty busy here, putting up factories, research centers and boring machinery, which they're using to dig into the ground and toward the tunnels. Despite heavy losses, we've managed to capture a base, mount turrets atop fixed platforms and start the production of robots. Unfortunately, our resources are very limited, so keep that in mind!
RobotsWin: Spectacular, <Player>!

Our congratulations! The island has been fully cleared. And it's good that you didn't fully destroy the kelleroid factories and research centers. We can retrofit the dominator structures, establish our own research base, and get to work. <Player>, you may return to the government building, where a warm reception awaits.

GovTextLoss: That's very sad, of course, but to tell you the truth it is on dominators that I have bet my annual salary. As expected, the intelligence based on software engineering and klissan technologies took the upper hand. Don't get me wrong, it's not like I support dominators. No, I just needed the money, badly. By the way, the prize -- a fairly large amount -- has already been sent to the dominator island. Four bags of cash in small bills, in local currency, ha-ha. Don't you think our billionaire is a little eccentric?

I almost feel a bit ill at ease... ...since it was through your efforts that I could make the money, and you have essentially risked your life for nothing. This isn't fair! Here's <Money> cr, they are yours now.

By the way, our restless billionaire is now launching yet another asini... umm... unusual project. This time he wants to ascertain which of the five major intelligent races in the Galaxy is best suited for surviving in absolute vacuum without special equipment. I think we should nominate dominators as a potential sixth race, ha-ha! And I'll bet on them again.
GovTextStart: Hmmmm.... I was asked to contact you specifically. Let's say you were recommended by someone as an experienced combat pilot. This is a fairly dangerous matter, and somewhat unusual too, but I am sure you'll be interested enough to at least hear me out.

A certain fairly eccentric gaal billionaire who is the biggest supporter of scientific research on our planet occasionally offers to fund certain... umm... let's call them brave and unusual experiments that seek to find perfection in a number of areas. This time around he is launching a certain... umm... project that has been popularly dubbed "Intuition and Improvisation vs Logic and Mathematics."

It's all very simple: here's you, and here are a few dominator clans. The participants of this so-called project find themselves together on an island. The outcome of your fight with the dominators will determine what is stronger: free will or mechanistic logic. The winner will get a substantial cash prize. Still, I fail to understand what use dominators may have for galactic credits. So, are you in?
GovTextWin: Congratulations! As expected, live brains took the upper hand in competition with intelligence based on software engineering and klissan technologies.
And by the way, the organizers established a prize of <Money> cr for the winner. That's what you are getting. Once again, congratulations!

You may be interested to know that our restless billionaire is now launching yet another asini... umm... unusual project. This time he wants to ascertain which of the five major intelligent races in the Galaxy is best suited for surviving in absolute vacuum without special equipment. There is already no shortage of maloq volunteers. Would you be interested in participating on behalf of your own race?
Well, a no is a no, I guess... By the way, I think we should nominate dominators as a potential sixth race, ha-ha! I will even bet my annual salary on them.
34.Name: Starship
RobotsLoss: Oh, dear! Is the positronic brain really smarter than the human one and do dominators constitute a new stage in the evolution of intelligent life? We will all die! We will all be enslaved by intelligent machines!

Well. Relax. Calm down. So what's the big deal, some loser couldn't handle a couple of dominators. And now they can't wait to meet that loser at the government building. Did you hear that, ranger? Hurry up!
RobotsStart: Great, you have arrived. By the way, they may have forgotten to warn you that the organizer of all this insanity firmly believes that the will to win and the ability to improvise typical of live intelligent creatures give them a threefold advantage. For that reason, you will have to fend off three groups of enemies to "even out" the chances. Your base will be centrally located in dominator-controlled areas, so try putting up proper defenses.
Good luck to you, ranger. You're going to need it.
RobotsWin: Give 'em hell! Ha-ha! Protein-based intelligence trumps positronic one. To be honest with you, I had no doubts whatsoever that you'd be able to handle it.
Now you have to run to the government building to claim your prize.

GovTextLoss: Hmmmm.... This is absolutely disgusting! Why did we even give you this mission? The ranger we used to hire before you always did a great job. We should have taken our business to him again. Yes, this is by far not the first dominator shock troop we shoot down on the orbit and force to make an emergency landing on this island. As you may guess, some of the trash is what's left over from previous dominator landings.
Take this <Money> cr. Even though you lost, you are still entitled to milk money -- milk helps purge radioactive isotopes from the body. Good luck!
GovTextStart: Do you have a radiation protection suit, <Player>? If not, I suggest you get one. As you have probably guessed by now, we propose that you travel to a fairly inhospitable place. Some time ago, our air defenses shot down a transport that happened to be teeming with dominators.

The ship crash landed on an island dump where they bring nuclear waste from all over the planet for disposal. It would be stupid to hope that radiation would damage dominator chips and systems, especially if one considers where they come from. On the other hand, we cannot ignore any dominators roaming our planet, so we suggest you go to that island and destroy the surviving dominators, turning them into piles of radioactive debris.
GovTextWin: Hmmmm.... Not bad, not bad at all. Still, it took the ranger we used to hire before you much less time to accomplish the mission, and the losses were smaller too. Yes, this is by far not the first dominator shock troop we shoot down on the orbit and force to make an emergency landing on this island. As you may guess, some of the trash is what's left over from previous dominator landings.
Regardless, you have honestly earned your <Money> cr. Here they are. And one other thing. May I suggest you have no X-rays taken any time soon? Good luck!
35.Name: Dump
35.RobotsLoss: Bah... With this kind of skill operating combat machines, it is shocking the dominators haven't buried you among piles of radioactive debris. They really let you have it, huh, ranger? My radiation detector readings went through the roof! Hurry up, they are already waiting for you at the government building.
RobotsStart: Welcome to our dump, <Player>! It's not too hot for you, is it? He-he. Radiation not too bright?

But back to the business at hand! Unfortunately, quite a few dominators managed to survive. They left behind their damaged ship and captured a number of plants. Not all of them though, luckily, so one of the plants will be at your disposal. Please try to use all available resources wisely. Good luck!
35.RobotsWin: Excellent! You really let them have it, huh, ranger? My radiation detector readings went through the roof! Hurry up, they are already waiting for you at the government building.

GovTextLoss: Alas... Your attempt to solve the problem in an environmentally responsible manner has gone nowhere. To be honest with you, I was the only one who believed you could be successful, and you let me down.
Nevertheless, you are being allowed <Money> from the veteran's fund. Here it is, sign here.
GovTextStart: When was the last time you went to a museum, ranger? I mean the museum of combat robots.

Not that you could call it a museum, of course. It's more like a giant cemetery. After the dominator rebellion, the Coalition's five races signed a treaty calling for decommission and destruction of all intelligent combat robots. The Arruga Island is now home to the most dangerous and destructive of them that were supposed to be sunk with the island itself. But just when our tectonic engineers began submerging the island a bunch of dominators showed up. It looks like they decided to lay their manipulators on our most dangerous robots, and we simply cannot afford to let this happen. We need your help.
If you can stop the dominators, we will not have to hit the island from the orbit, and our planet's environment will be saved.
GovTextWin: Excellent job, ranger! To be honest with you, we have begun considering a strike from the orbit since we did not quite believe your mission would be a success. By the way, I have just been informed that the dominators managed to activate one of the robots. Luckily, the pirated software installed on it by greedy pelengs crashed at the most inopportune moment. Otherwise you and I wouldn't be talking right now. So, apparently, even pirates serve a purpose at times.

Here's your <Money> cr. By the way, could I interest you in buying some peleng-made automatic swamp harvesters? Whatever their reasons, the pelengs sold them to us at a 70% discount, so you can really have them for a pittance.
36.Name: Sinking Island
36.RobotsLoss: You lost! You need to leave the island ASAP since now we will be forced to launch a strike from space to destroy both the dominators and our own combat equipment, whether the environmentalists like it or not. You are being expected at the government building.
RobotsStart: Greetings, ranger! The situation is totally out of control. The dominators have taken over most of the key sectors. Fortunately, we managed to clear a small island for you and set up a production facility there. We suggest you organize your defenses right away since the dominators have already discovered our presence. Be especially wary of the blazeroids that have arrived at the island first and had sufficient time to settle in. You won't be able to dislodge them with an ad hoc spontaneous assault. Good luck!
And one other thing. Don't worry about the dominators launching any of our own equipment dumped on the island. All the key components have been removed from these robots or destroyed.
36.RobotsWin: You did it! Now you need to evacuate the island since we will resume our efforts to submerge it. Dominators or not, we need to complete the disposal effort. You are expected at the government building.

GovTextLoss: Disgusting. Do you even realize that now the microscopic herring roe industry on our planet is doomed before ever having had any chances to take off? This is a total disaster that will cost billions, and hundreds of thousands of gourmet food lovers all over the Galaxy will never even know what you have deprived them of.

And this doesn't even account for the loss of the experimental plant and all the valuable equipment. In all fairness, you should have been made to pay restitution, but instead those bureaucrats are giving you a bonus! Naturally, you will not be receiving your agreed upon fee; however, I am obligated to pay you a bonus of <Money> cr, which goes against every one of my own moral principles. Now get out of here, I don't want to ever see you again.
GovTextStart: Yes, <Player>, your help would be very much appreciated. We have recently received an alarming report from one of our bottom research submarines that detected dominators in sector 209B, at the depth of 4 miles. The ship has never been heard of again or responded to our communications. We checked our secret archives and found out that it was in that very sector that an experimental underwater microscopic herring farm was mothballed eons ago. It must have been taken over by the dominators.

Those bastards have now laid their filthy manipulators on our experimental precision underwater equipment. Do you even realize what the dominators could use that farm equipment for if you don't stop them? If you take this mission, we will give you a few combat robots and help you access the station. If you manage to liberate the station, you will definitely get a reward.
GovTextWin: By gosh and by microscopic herring, that's great! You did it! Now that your valiant fight with our "invited" dominators has become public knowledge, we can restart our program to raise microscopic herring. That was some plan, huh? Well, yes, we kept you in the dark, but we took a heck of a risk too by luring the dominators into the experimental station full of expensive equipment.

You have truly earned your <Money> cr. It isn't a small sum, but I am all too happy to pay it since our prospective revenue from selling microscopic herring roe will cover every expense many times over.
37.Name: Depth
37.RobotsLoss: What a sorry sight, ranger! Station demolished, expensive equipment destroyed and dominators still in control! A submarine is already standing by to bring you back to the mainland, but you should really hope it sinks on the way. You see, we only honor winners here, and losers, well, let's just say no one is too fond of them.
37.RobotsStart: Well, <Player>, you have successfully disembarked at the station. Now it's all up to you. We installed monitoring gauges on the hull and determined that there are dominators of all three types present at the station. So yes, it will get real hot here. I suggest you try to provoke a fight between blazeroids and terronoids and use the ensuing confusion to wrestle a plant back from one of the two. Otherwise, you won't last long without resources. Good luck!
37.RobotsWin: Excellent job! Not even our precious equipment got damaged! You are a true ace, ranger. Hurry up, a submarine is waiting to take you back to the government building for an after action report.

GovTextLoss: Hmmmm.... On the one hand, you should be properly punished, since your failure puts hundreds upon hundreds of thousands of lives in danger. On the other, I began covering my bets early by buying up lead. Now all we need is a tiny little bit of a leak about a reactor falling into dominators' dirty grabbers and lead prices will shoot through the roof. Then I'll really make a killing.

So, long story short, I've even decided to pay you a bonus as my true benefactor. I'll give you a choice: <Money> cr or an equivalent in lead at yesterday's price. In a few days, you'll be able to sell it for ten times the amount! So, what do you say? All right, money it is. I'll go transfer it right away.
GovTextStart: Just curious, have you ever been to any "hot" spots? Like, say, a nuclear waste dump or a reactor core? If you haven't, may I recommend visiting -- that's a thrill of your life! Come to think of it, it is such a pity they now consider nuclear power plants obsolete. Whatever their benefits, new, safe orbital power plants don't even have a fraction of the old romantic appeal.

But let's get to the point. We have an inactive reactor on one of the islands that was mothballed hundreds of years ago. The background radiation level there is quite safe. Dominators would be your much bigger worry. They have recently landed on that island, dismantled the outer protective walls and seem to be trying to restart the reactor. At the same time, they are making some very suspicious modifications and improvements. Our analysts believe that the dominators have found a way to increase the reactor yield substantially.

You must stop them, since apparently they are not going to use the reactor to supply heat and power to our cities. Once they have a high-yield working plant at their disposal, they may want to supply us with so much heat and power that half the cities on this planet will simply cease to exist.
GovTextWin: Great, I am glad you lived up to my expectations. Because some unscrupulous scaremongers here launched a real run on the metals market, buying up lead and spreading panic. Someone in the government must have leaked information. We will definitely find the culprit, since not so many knew about it.
And you have honestly earned your <Money> cr and my compliments.
38.Name: Reactor
38.RobotsLoss: I am afraid your failure means that all of us are now facing a potential multimegaton nuclear explosion, courtesy of the dominators. It looks like lead will be more expensive than gold soon. I bet our government officials can't wait to talk to you heart to heart. Hurry up!
RobotsStart: Just a tad longer, and it would have been too late, ranger. What took you so long?

We have barely managed to hold on to that base we wrestled away from the dominators before your arrival. Luckily, the dominators threw all they had at us, thus having to leave a number of production facilities alone. Try to beat them to all those plants.
38.RobotsWin: Phew... You truly did the impossible, ranger, and the populace of the planet will be forever grateful. Still, I bet you'll be much more excited about the cash reward that is awaiting you at the government building. Hurry up, they are expecting you.

GovTextLoss: Incredible! That was some snafu all right -- landing on a wrong island and falling straight into dominator lap! And your competitors are still waiting for you and the filming crew on the next island up. The TV crew are already on their way there, but it's not going to help you become a movie star. Not after that lackluster fight with the dominators anyway.

Regardless, there's still a little cash in it for you courtesy of our sponsor, the Chemical and Biological Weapons Plant, that established a consolation prize of <Money> cr for the most spectacular loser. The Chemical and Biological Weapons Plant. Only our Live Bio-Yogurt Cultures Are Truly Alive and Truly Cultured!
GovTextStart: Oh, what a character! Turn sideways. Now, a frontal shot. Here, take this number. Say something menacing. Your wallet or your life, maybe? You can always tell one of your own humanoids. You fit the bill perfectly -- what we need for this shoot is an absolute wacko who wouldn't give a hoot about the lives of others.

Our chemical and biological weapons plant is teetering on the brink of bankruptcy. They decided to use the last of their cash to fund a reality show - "The Island of Death", it's shaping up to become a real blockbuster. The script is a work of genius: a few participants are sent to an island where they use giant combat robots to fight for survival. The last man standing will receive a substantial cash prize and the title "Conqueror of Death". Make up your mind. Here's you chance to prove you are the best of the best!
GovTextWin: Umm... we've had us a little snafu here. We kind of made a mistake and delivered you and the film crew to a totally different island that happens to be controlled by dominators. And your competitors are still waiting for you and the film crew on the next island up. Fortunately, the footage filmed captivated the audience like never before, the channel's ratings shot up through the roof, and they have already greenlit a full season. So we sent a second crew to film the rest of the competitors on that other island. No one even realized that you were fighting dominators.

By the way, we are launching another show and would like to invite you to participate as an accomplished star. The Cold, that's the show's working name. Imagine, twenty individuals are grabbed off the street, stuffed into duffel bags and taken to the north pole to be hunted by wild animals, cannibal maloqs and rabid penguins. Over time, stronger competitors eat up their weaker fellow sufferers, and the final survivor gets a million credits and a nasty pneumonia. Not interested? Then here's your <Money> cr. Sign here.
39.Name: Reality Show
39.RobotsLoss: Wait! Cut! I think we are on the wrong island! It isn't the other competitors you are fighting, <Player>, it's dominators! And it looks like you've lost already. We just can't use that for the show. We are done here, and you are fired, ranger. You are a lousy fighter, you just can't give us the right thrill we want for this show.
RobotsStart: Welcome to Hell! Damn, I mixed up my lines! Where was it... Ah, here. "Whose armor is all rusted out, whose aim is three yards off, who is weaker..." Damn it! That's also for a different show! Oh, I got it!

Here it is, our island of death. Other competitors have long arrived and took up their positions. We are only waiting for you, <Player>! Give each other your all! Build bigger robots, more weapons of mass destruction, more bombs and hotter flames! Let the ground shudder, the water boil out and the competitor plants crumble to dust! There will only be one last man standing! And let the strongest man win!
39.RobotsWin: Stop! And cut! Congratulations, you are the only survivor! Had your competitors been able to write and signed the contract, their families would have received 10,000 credits each as a death benefit. Hurry up, your reward and a rabid mob of fans are waiting for you.

40.GovTextLoss: Umm, <Player>, you are kind of pale! It's all right, winning is not important. What matters is fighting bravely and to the end. Your bravery has just earned you <Money> cr. And one other thing. For your own good, you'd better get off this planet ASAP. If the miners learn you were responsible for their increased production quotas, they will eat you alive. And I am not speaking me-pha-to-ri-cal-ly, or whatever that word is.
GovTextStart: Uh-huh, we've got us this little problem, and I think you could help us out. Our shipbuilding plants have recently completed a new great feat of maloq engineering -- a megadrill. It's this giant rig for deep drilling. But before they could even assemble the rig on site, kelleroids shot down the escorts, took over the tugboat and towed the rig to an island they've captured. Faeyan experts have determined that the dominators are looking for some deep me-ta-pho-ric in-tru-sion po-ly-plast... damn, what a tongue twister! In a nutshell, these bores are boring their holes with our very own bore.

We can't get to them by air since their air defenses are excellent. We will send you over aboard a submarine. It will also deliver a mobile production facility to the rig along with some robots. You will be in charge of it all. What are you waiting for? Get on with it. Oh, I forgot. We will pay you a nice chunk of cash if you deliver.
40.GovTextWin: Now, that's a great job! It looks like everyone is happy: dominators have been destroyed, our miners got their drill back, those faeyan sissies found their in-tru-... ah, whatever, so they have no reason to complain either. What did you say? Money? Oh, yes! Here is your <Money> cr.
40.Name: Megadrill
40.RobotsLoss: Defeat? I wouldn't want to be you now, <Player>! Now, on the double, get your sorry butt to the government building, they'll set you straight there.
RobotsStart: All hands on deck! While we were in transit, blazeroids have landed on the island. I don't know if they are after our drill or simply want to kick the kelleroids off the island, but either way we need to stay sharp.

Now the good news. The mobile production facility has been set up and started. It is at your disposal now. And the hackers the faeyans sent managed to disable the main kelleroid gun and immobilize their platform. All you have left to do is blow them all to smithereens.
40.RobotsWin: Bravo, Ranger <Ranger>! You have executed a flawless textbook assault, as if it were a demonstration at the Military Academy. The drill will be recovered and used to mine titanium for the military industry. Very soon, helicopters will bring faeyan scientists over and pick you up on the way back. For the time being, kick back a little, or better yet brush up on your Service Manual.

41.GovTextLoss: Seven reconnaissance squads and hundreds of industrial spies have been working on this -- and now it's all down the drain! Ranger <Player>, you are an idiot. A firing squad would be too easy for you, they gotta make you endure gaalian lectures! But hey, at least someone is happy with your incompetence: the association of battery manufacturers and importers is giving you a prize of <Money> cr. By the way, if you had won the government would have paid you way more.
GovTextStart: Wait, I need to change the battery here. You see, our planet has virtually no sources of energy of its own; we use imported batteries.

But it's going to change now. Our great scientists sto... I mean developed a revolutionary technology for supercooled thermonuclear fusion and just finished building our first reactor. But they hardly had time enough to figure out how it all worked before kelleroids descended upon the island. They may have been drawn in by the energetic emissions from the power source. Just imagine, they started the reactor and are now stealing our energy. What has the world come to? -- dominators stealing from pelengs! We are not going to put up with this.
If you agree to destroy these dominators, we will take you to a luxurious resort island and make first rate production facilities available to you. Say yes, we are even going to pay you for it.
GovTextWin: That's a mission well accomplished, <Player>. You are getting <Money> cr for delivering secret cargo. Peleng society will never forget you.

What power plant? Remember, we have never built any power plants. Officially, that island doesn't even exist. If you ever say a word about this... Dzuhallag has ears everywhere. The official story is that you have transported some cargo from point A to point B. It's a standard procedure.
41.Name: Cold Fusion
RobotsLoss: Defeat?! No, this cannot be!
You... you... do you even understand what kind of a debt hole we have dug ourselves into to build that island, that reactor and the orbital transmitter? Report to the government building immediately.
RobotsStart: Well, here it is, our subtropical paradise. Naturally, the reactor did affect the climate somewhat, but the beaches are still great and as snow white as we promised you.
Terronoids have also landed here, so it is going to be a hard battle. The government has allocated you a large supply of batteries -- mi acumulador e su acumulador, so to speak.
Good luck to you! Don't catch any colds.
41.RobotsWin: Long live great Ranger <Player>! You have turned our precious power plant back to us and ensured we have a supply of virtually free energy for years to come. They can't wait to see you at the government building and hear your report.

42.GovTextLoss: Get out of my sight! You are not worthy of being called a ranger since it is your fault that our economy is once again dependent on imported germanium. This amount of <Money> cr comes to you courtesy of General Ellamory himself as a sign of his appreciation for your resolve to fight to the very end. But had you accomplished your mission successfully, the payout would have been much larger.
GovTextStart: Let me give you a brief rundown of the situation. Some time ago a germanium-rich meteorite fell on our planet. This mineral is badly needed by our semiconductor industry, but it is even more valuable for dominators. They have already taken over most of the island.

If you agree to take on these dominators and rid our planet of the entire lot we will provide you with a first rate production facility to build combat robots. Naturally, we will also pay you an attractive compensation for your efforts.
42.GovTextWin: The General is absolutely delighted with your tactics, and most of our analysts agree with him. We now have access to a cheap source of germanium, and that means that very soon our goods will be substantially cheaper and more profitable. The Association of Semiconductor Equipment Manufacturers even wrote you a check in the amount of <Money> cr, which it is my pleasure to pass along to you.
42.Name: Crater
42.RobotsLoss: What a pity! I hope you have learned your lesson from all of this. One way or another, our air force will soon level this island, and you will now have to explain it to the government why planet <Planet> is not going to get any cheap germanium.
RobotsStart: The situation is as follows: terronoids have done a good job of digging in inside the crater and captured one of our bases that brave General Ellamory's soldiers managed to build while his other troops were repelling attacks by blazeroids that unexpectedly descended upon the area. The General's army executed an orderly withdrawal to its fall-back positions; however they did manage to mothball one of its bases that you will now have at your disposal.
General Ellamory recommends that you pay particular attention to terronoid robots since they know the theater well and are quite aggressive. Good luck, <Player>!
42.RobotsWin: Splendid! The crater's been cleared. Our engineers are already on the way to start developing the deposit, and you are expected at the government building.

43.GovTextLoss: Only your victories over dominators saved your hide from the explosive grabber. You couldn't have commanded your robots in a more asinine manner. But to be fair, you did not flee like a coward and stood your ground to the end. For this, you deserve a small reward -- <Money> cr. And quit looking at me like that. Had you accomplished your mission successfully, the payout would have been much larger. And now, DIS-MISSED!
GovTextStart: Do you even know how difficult it is to maintain a combat-ready army? No, you don't. We maloqs build special training grounds for this, so that our soldiers could learn to kill practicing on robot mock-ups, gain combat experience and vent their rage.

So, what was I talking about? Oh, yes! Not so long ago, Maloqsoft Corporation gave us a gift -- brand new training grounds. They have also gotten a good deal on dominator mock-ups from the pelengs and set up an effective lighting scheme for key areas using fixtures deployed in space. The place will be a boon for our valiant soldiers -- brave but not very experienced yet. Keeping in mind Maloqsoft's great reputation, we decided to let you test our new grounds first so as not to put the lives... I mean, combat experience of our soldiers at risk. Make up your mind, <Player>! We will even pay you for that.
43.GovTextWin: This is wonderful! There is no better sight for a maloq than dead bodies stacked up high... that is, piles of destroyed enemy equipment, of course. Maloqsoft has already established a cash reward of <Money> cr for saving the grounds. And we have already sorted out the pelengs too. This human shyster of ours will make sure they pay for the damage, even if that means giving us the shirt off their back. What did they expect sticking us with an unlicensed version of training software to run their mock-ups?
43.Name: Maloqsoft
43.RobotsLoss: You stinky turducken of an independent contractor! How dare you wear the ranger uniform! Bungle an easy assignment such as this one? How about we leave you right here while the air force bombs the bejesus out of this place? Oh, all right, we'll save you for the government types, they want a crack at you too.
43.RobotsStart: This is a provocation! Those are real dominators, not mock-ups! Ranger <Player>, begin mopping up the training grounds immediately before those infernal contraptions begin multiplying like rabbits. We cannot allow this marvel of military engineering to fall into the hands of the machines. If you decide you cannot handle it yourself, call in air support and we will blow this place sky high and be done with it altogether. Now get on with it!
43.RobotsWin: Way to go, <Player>! You fought with honor! Your assault tactics belong in a textbook, and some of your most eloquent language has acquired a life of its own among our officers. Get some sleep and then report to the government building for an award ceremony.

44.GovTextLoss: Ranger <Player>, you are in violation of your contract. Indeed, we held you up as an honest humanoid, and now here you are, turning around and cheating us. I am afraid you are going to be here a while -- we have filed a claim against you in court seeking substantial damages, and the case is now pending. On the other hand, hold on a sec, let me have another look... Damn bureaucrats! Why didn't they make the small print even smaller? Oh, all right, we'll make a partial payment to you in the amount of <Money> cr, since you did make a nominal effort to fight as set forth in the contract.
GovTextStart: <Player>, if you ever heard of Mauna Roa, you must know that it is the most luxurious and expensive resort in the entire Galaxy, and only the rich and the famous can afford to vacation there. It's a huge mountain in the middle of the ocean where you can ski from the top straight to the beach at the foot.

And of course it is quite a cash cow, or rather it used to be before dominators descended upon it and all the tourists had to be evacuated. Whatever it is the machines want with it, the invasion has caused us a great financial loss. <Player>, we need you to realize the depth of our suffering here. We ask you to help us free the island, and naturally, we are going to make it worth your while.
44.GovTextWin: That was a fantastic job you did, <Player>! If all merchants fought so well, we'd make short work of the dominators. By the way, we found out what it was the terronoids were mining for. It was silver they needed for electronic components of their ships. And now it will cover all our losses and costs. Even paying you <Money> cr wouldn't set us back by all that much. By the way, here's your money. Sign here.
44.Name: Mauna Roa Beaches
44.RobotsLoss: This is a total disaster! It is even worse than the stock market crash of two years ago. Ranger <Player>, you have let us down big time. Now the island will be handled by the military, and we all know what that means: radiation, craters, chemical weapons and other such nice things. Goodbye, our luxurious island resort!
RobotsStart: As you can see, the situation is quite complicated:

Terronoids that have landed first dug into the mountain seeking cover from the ranger bombers we have hired. Then they burrowed a hole straight to our own airfield and destroyed all our air assets on the ground. After that, they deployed some kind of mechanical bugs all over the island that jam the navigational systems of our cruise missiles and went about mining some rocks from under the mountain. Then, just before you arrived, blazeroids descended upon the island, pushed the terronoids away from most of the coastal areas and made an all-out attempt to dislodge them from the mountain as well.
We are making available to you a great operations base, a number of production facilities and substantial resources. We are not going to penny pinch you where it matters.
44.RobotsWin: Splendid! We now control the island again. We are sending emergency crews down to restore the infrastructure and build new resorts. As for you, <Player>, you are being expected at the government building with an after action report. However, feel free to take some time first to relax on the beach you have fought so valiantly to retake.

45.GovTextLoss: I just knew I shouldn't have trusted a ranger with this job. Your inept command led to a planetary disaster of epic proportions, and now it's me they will hold responsible for it. Besides, not only am I the fall guy now as the person in charge of this mess, but I also have to pay you <Money> cr -- the "danger money." Yeah, danger my butt! By the way, had you accomplished your mission, the payout would have been much larger, and our planet wouldn't have been on the brink of an environmental disaster.
GovTextStart: How about some coffee, <Player>?

No? All right then, it's not like we drink much of that sludge ourselves. You see, we have a serious problem with potable water, or rather a lack thereof. Many years ago, our planet was very rich in mineral resources, but we wasted them all gratuitously and now have nothing left. Our scientists came up with a fairly attractive program for recycling and reusing trash. Sounds incredible, doesn't it? Nevertheless, we did manage to build recycling facilities in the Trash Valley -- our planet's largest dump -- and the results are quite promising.

Unfortunately, our plants and the treasure trove of recycled resources concentrated at one location caught the attention of dominators. A huge army of battered blazeroids, terronoids and kelleroids descended upon the valley. They captured our plants, reequipped them and now use them to repair themselves. They scrapped all scrubbers and other environment protection systems. It took these dominators a few short weeks to push our planet to the brink of a true environmental disaster. Our water is all poisoned, the ozone layer is getting thinner by the minute, and entire species of animals become extinct.

We beg you to help us get rid of the dominators. What's at stake here is the health... heck, the very existence of our entire planet! We will assist you in any way we can and pay you handsomely for your troubles.
45.GovTextWin: Bravo, <Player>, bravo! Not only has our planet been saved from an environmental disaster, but we now also have sufficient resources for decades to come since dominator plants could be easily optimized for large scale recycling, and broken robots could be utilized as well. But it's not like we are forgetting about you here. Judging by how green your face has turned, it's either you are a peleng, or your health suffered badly during your sojourn into the Trash Valley. Either way, we are going to pay you <Money> cr so that you could get proper treatment. Get some well-deserved rest. And let me shake your hand before you go. We will always remember what you did for us.
45.Name: Trash
45.RobotsLoss: This is a total disaster! Toxic waste is about to spill outside the valley, and the entire planet will get contaminated! Get out of here, you will only impede our efforts to evacuate civilians from dangerous areas.
45.RobotsStart: Greetings, ranger! I think you can now see for yourself what is going on here. Our water is already contaminated with toxic waste and fumes. It is now unusable, and the marine life is becoming extinct. We do not recommend you come anywhere near the water... Or better yet, keep your space suit on at all times. You see, even the air here is polluted with dangerous fumes, and unless you destroy the dominators a similar fate will befall our entire planet. Hurry!
45.RobotsWin: Splendid! Our environmental experts have already begun cleaning up contaminated areas while engineers are out in force studying the factories modified by the dominators. As for you, <Player>, you are expected at the government building right away where our prominent politicians would like to thank you in person. They hope to earn some additional political capital by shaking your heroic hand in front of the stereocameras. But hey, I never told you that.

GovTextLoss: We are really sorry the mission has failed. The station's self-destruct system will now kick in, and many months of hard work will go to waste. We are not blaming you since this was a very difficult mission. We are giving you a bonus of <Money> cr in recognition of your bravery.
Of course, this isn't much, but all our resources will go to cover a new program to study the virus.
GovTextStart: We have a very important mission for you, <Player>! You may have heard of the recent epidemic of arboreous flu that cost thousands of humans their lives. The interplanetary Yellow Cross took it upon themselves to develop a vaccine, and we offered one of our uninhabited islands as a site for the laboratory so that the experimental virus strains would remain safely confined.

Unfortunately, <Player>, we were unable to maintain sufficient secrecy. Dominators learned about the project and landed on the island. Blazeroid earth moving equipment is already on the way to our laboratories. We suggest you take command of the combat robots purchased specifically for this mission and stop the dominators. The fate of humanity is at stake since the epidemic will wreak unimaginable havoc if the vaccine is not developed. And if the dominators succeed in laying their hands on a mutant virus that could affect other races... Long story short, you are our only hope.
46.GovTextWin: <Player>, let your path of benevolence and humanism be clear and serene! You could help stop the epidemic and save the lives of millions. Your name will be entered in the roster of the Yellow Cross' honorary allies. <Money> cr will be but a symbolic token of our appreciation since money is nothing, and what really matters is harmony and purity of thought.
46.Name: Virus
RobotsLoss: What did you do?! Your defeat put our efforts to create the vaccine at risk! And quite possibly, all of the intelligent biological life in this Galaxy is now in grave danger.
And to think that we put so much trust in you!
RobotsStart: You came right on time. Blazeroids have landed at three different locations simultaneously, and while we were fighting our way down kelleroids captured the teleportation station on top and brought in plenty of their own stormtroopers.
The situation is aggravated even further by our inability to call in reinforcements. Fortunately, the dominators have not yet taken over production facilities. Try to beat them to those plants.
46.RobotsWin: You did it! Good job, <Player>! Today you saved the lives of millions of patients. This selfless feat has not only earned you a financial reward, you now have the sincere gratitude and respect of the entire gaal race.

GovTextLoss: Execute him!

Wait, where are you going? You rangers don't have any sense of humor at all, do you? Don't worry, the worst that can happen to you is you'll get fined. Wait, let me tally the damage... Secretary, what's the story on the armor alloy plant?

Incredible! As a matter of fact, we have actually made money on this disaster. The insurance will cover replacement costs, penalties, etc. Hey, there's even enough left over to pay you <Money> cr. And now, DIS-MISSED!
GovTextStart: You, <Player>, are exactly the kind of specialist we need. You are not a pirate or some kind of merchant; you are a true warrior, so you can understand the gravity of the problem we face.

So here goes. Our planet is home to the largest armor alloy manufacturer in the sector that caters to the needs of the defense industry. Our alloys are used to build the best battle ships in the galaxy. However, when the planet was liberated we realized it to our horror that our main production facility had been captured by dominators. It appears they could also use the best armor in the galaxy. Do you understand what would happen if our army loses access to these alloys? It would be a disaster! Deploy to the coastal shelf immediately -- that's where the plant is located -- and stop these dang tin cans.
47.GovTextWin: That was a great battle! It was broadcast to military units all over the planet, and I must admit our officers and men learned quite a few things from you. And that the plant is now working for us is the best news of the decade. On behalf of planet <Planet>, it is my pleasure to pay you this <Money> cr for the invaluable assistance you rendered our military-industrial complex.
47.Name: Mines
RobotsLoss: What a mess! How could you? This is the end!

To prevent dominators from producing advanced armored hulls we will now have to destroy the facility from the air. It's such a damn waste! And you, ranger, your only hope is for the evacuation helicopters to arrive ahead of the bombers.
47.RobotsStart: You made the right decision, <Player>! Let me give you a sitrep: heavy fighting is ongoing on the territory of the facility between blazeroids that control most of the furnaces and terronoids that are holding a position in the extreme south. Our assault troops captured a kelleroid base and a number of adjoining plants, so you are not going to have to start from scratch. And now go and turn all this dumb, soulless metal into scrap!
47.RobotsWin: Long live great Ranger <Player>! You did it! Our system's military will be eternally grateful to you. Our high command is waiting for your report at the government building.

48.GovTextLoss: Unfortunately, by taking on this mission you bit off more than you could chew. But then again, when hiring you we essentially hoped for a miracle. Now the only way to destroy the dominators on the island would be by indiscriminate aerial bombing. God willing, this will do them in. By the way, since you stood your ground so valiantly until the very end, we decided to pay you <Money> cr to compensate you for your efforts, even though this is just a small fraction of what you could have received had you accomplished your mission successfully.
48.GovTextStart: Salaam, <Player>! We need you. No, no, you are not wanted by the authorities here, nor do we wish to throw you in jail or collect an unpaid debt from you. We are in need of your strategic potential. Yes, you guessed right -- dominators have descended upon our planet and began terrorizing the Al-Kagul Island. Have you heard of it? No big deal, it's perfectly all right for an alien. This is the blessed patch of land where the wisest dervishes and mullahs spend their time getting to know themselves and God through their hermitage, prayers and labor. Now, speaking of labor. Since the only two crops growing on the island are date trees and grapes, the hermits make their living exporting their homemade wine. The local community has become so efficient producing that good beverage that cheers that revenues from the sale thereof now make for a substantial part of our planet's gross domestic product. But everything went down the drain when the island was attacked and captured by all three dominator types at the same time. Most of the community managed to take cover in the cellars, and official mourning is now being observed over those who didn't. While fighting each other, the machines have transformed the once bountiful oasis beyond recognition. They completely rebuilt the port and destroyed most of the vines and some of the date groves during battle. I am not going to bother telling you about the damage to the state treasury or the dangers befalling thousands of noble hermits. Instead, I am going to offer you something that is sure going to compel you to take part in the operation -- money. A lot of money.
48.GovTextWin: A thousand blessings, <Player>! Our prayers have been heard! The Great One sent us you as His agent and expelled the mechanical beasts from the great valleys of Al-Kagul. And, naturally, the renewed production and exports of alcohol will help ensure our well-being. Yours too -- to the tune of <Money> cr.
48.Name: Al-Kagul
48.RobotsLoss: Your defeat is very unfortunate, but it could well be expected. Deep down inside, we were prepared for the loss of our beautiful island. Well, we will evacuate the survivors from their bunkers in a few days, and you will also be picked up by a helicopter soon.
48.RobotsStart: Once again - Salaam to you, ranger. As you can see, the situation is very dire: you only control the fortified section of the mountain and a small trek while the dominators are successfully taking over production facilities sabotaged by our forces right before your arrival. Your main opponents, kelleroids, are holding the checkpoint at the entrance to the harbor; terronoids took over a former pier and transformed it beyond any recognition while blazeroids now occupy the blooming oases in the north. The tactical position of our base is very unfavorable, and you will not survive a joint attack by all the three types. Try to pit two of your opponents against each other and fight on a single front. That's what our analysts are recommending.
48.RobotsWin: Amazing! You have done the impossible -- just when faeyan analysts were predicting your mission to be a complete failure. There's no doubt the Great One intervened in the battle and guided your hand to victory so that you could save His devoted followers. Just wait a few minutes longer. The evacuation crew is already on the way.

49.GovTextLoss: You have let us down, <Player>, even though our analysts gave you a 79.451% chance of success. Now we will need to resort to Plan C and dispatch <clr>Boris Willis<clrEnd> and his drillers to blow up the planetoid from within. It is such a pity since this would be a great place to conduct research and an excellent forward observatory. Still, we should not underestimate your efforts since you bravely defended the base to the very end and never gave in. For that, you deserve <Money> cr. Yes, it isn't much, but you did fail the mission.
49.GovTextStart: Ranger <Player>, please use whatever analytic abilities you may have to properly understand the mission. Following a number of unsuccessful attempts to occupy our system, blazeroids decided to use a weapon capable of destroying life on one of the planets in its entirety for hope that this would demoralize our armed forces. They assembled an outsized Gnuuk gravitational engine on the Oort-Yantalaki planetoid MK-10046 and gave it a powerful impetus directed against the vector of its movement. As a result, the planetoid became unstable and shifted to a hyperbolic trajectory projected to traverse the orbit of our planet in a point where it would be captured by its gravitational field with a probability of 87.329%, thus resulting in a likely collision. When the two bodies collide, the planetoid will explode, with the shock wave and thermal effects destroying 99.957% of the population of planet <Planet>. Naturally, such an outcome is absolutely unacceptable. We are considering a number of options to prevent this crisis, of which one would involve taking over the island on the planetoid where the Gnuuk engine has been set up. Basically, that's what we need you for since we do not have any strategists on staff on this planet, and it would take an expert sent by the Galactic Council over a month to get here. What do you say, Ranger <Player>? How about you prove you are a truly intelligent person who can think straight?
49.GovTextWin: Great job, <Player>! Now we will not have to send <clr>Boris Willis<clrEnd> and his gang of human drillers to blow up this valuable planetoid. It makes it all the better that now we have a brand new observatory at our disposal and a source of uranium ore. I think you have earned this <Money> cr in good faith. If you ever need a job, please contact us. You will always be welcome here.
49.Name: Armageddong
49.RobotsLoss: What? You lost? No, I will not survive this! Oh, never mind the death of the planet, we have a plan B for that! I will never survive the loss of such a fantastic telescope. What are you still doing here? You are expected by the government.
49.RobotsStart: The portable teleporter left behind by the previous expedition comes very handy. Oh, nobody told you of the previous expedition? If you are interested in its fate you can explore the ruins to the south of our base. Unlike most other bodies of the Oort-Yantalaki type, this planetoid has a powerful gravitational field, an atmosphere and a hydrocarbon ocean that covers 87.345% of its surface. The remaining 12.655% are frigid islands covered with frozen water, ammonia and dry ice. A preliminary survey indicates that the planetoid may have a heavy uranium or thorium core. Such an object would certainly merit further research and has long been studied by the Keller series dominators. They have built an entire seismic analysis lab complex and an observatory featuring a radio interferometer array and a 70-meter reflector. It's a damn work of art! Blazeroids have already dug in inside a mountain in the northern part of the island where they are believed to have hidden the Gnuuk engine. Once you capture their base, our experts would start the engine in reverse to stabilize the planetoid's orbit. Don't forget about the kelleroids either -- their observatory would serve our planet <Planet> well.
49.RobotsWin: This is amazing! Truly remarkable! What does your victory have to do with it? I am simply admiring this fantastic reflector. Can you imagine, it allows for observing sources with an angular resolution of as little as 0.000065... Oh, yes, you can return to the planet. They are already waiting for you at the government building.

50.GovTextLoss: Aren't you ashamed of yourself, <Player>? Your inept command has pushed the entire planet to the brink of disaster. Any moment now, beta-terron will begin transforming the planet, and there's not a damn thing we can do about it. If it were not for that contract! Here. Disgusted that I am, I am still obligated to pay you <Money> cr. And now get out of here.
GovTextStart: Ah, <Player>, you couldn't have come at a better moment! Our Underground Mole operation is in its final stage and we need a strategic command expert. That would be you. Oh, yes, you are not yet privy to this secret information. Back during the Klissan War, human scientists went about developing a neutron weapon that could strike at crystalline klissan organisms. One of their research centers was located deep inside a bunker on our planet. Unfortunately, it was captured by the enemy at the most inopportune moment. Among other things, they managed to locate the bunker and used a neutrino impulse to detonate a prototype neutron bomb that had been assembled on the upper floors of the structure. With all hands lost, the reactor destroyed, and the station completely out of commission, everyone put the facility out of their minds for a long time. Until today, that is.

Dominators of two types simultaneously descended upon our planet and quickly proceeded to burrow tunnels to the ancient bunker. It is most likely that the machines have been attracted by the strange signals emitted from the deep. The bigger danger, however, is that they may find surviving neutron weapon designs they have not been aware of before. I hope you understand what that would mean for all the organic races of the Coalition. However, not everything is doom and gloom. Using an old ventilation shaft, we managed to deploy substantial forces inside the bunker and even built well-fortified bases there. By the time the blazeroids finished digging their tunnel and the kelleroids built their teleport, our forces were well in position to repel them. By the way, the bunker appeared to be full of robots with green markings that came from nowhere and made quite a nuisance of themselves for a while. What is especially remarkable is that as we examined some of the captured robots, it turned out they were not terronoids at all. For lack of anything better, we called that new series beta-terron. We have also discovered how these beta-terronoids came to be, but this is the kind of information we will be able to share with you only on site. Now let's get down to business. Heavy fighting exhausted both us and the beta-terronoids, and that was when blazeroids and kelleroids descended in force. Long story short, we need your help.
50.GovTextWin: Well, well, <Player>! It is not just some kind of robots that you have destroyed today, but an entire nascent dominator race, for which you deserve full credit. However, I hope you understand the importance of keeping this knowledge to yourself. God forbid the Galactic Council learns the human congress has almost caused an entire new series to develop. And to make it easier for you to keep your silence, we will pay you <Money> cr.
50.Name: Bunker
50.RobotsLoss: Goddammit, ranger! Look at what you did! Do you even know what it will be like to organize another assault? If it were not in the contract, we wouldn't even bother sending grave diggers for you.
50.RobotsStart: You are finally here! While you were in transit, kelleroids and blazeroids finished digging their tunnels to our base. The enemy is now at the gates! Despite all our efforts, we were also unable to hold on to the bunker's central room even though we did manage to delete the software controlling the plants. Thank God for small favors! But our mission here is not just to clear the bunker. Our main target is the central server of the beta-terron series. Just as on Gralgar, this series evolved when some of the modular robots began interacting with the klissan protoplasm under the influence of intense radiation. Now, where did all this stuff come from, you may ask. It is actually quite simple. When disaster hit, the reactor was at the acceleration stage, and once all the staff perished, there was no one left to stop the acceleration. The reactor blew up, and nuclear waste trickled down to the lower levels along with the protoplasm from the destroyed reservoirs. It was there, on the lower levels, that we kept our modular robots. You see, not only maloqs kept some of the old robot systems in storage. And since these modular robots had procreation algorithms programmed into them as a priority task, our local dominators followed the terronoid evolutionary path to a tee. Naturally, our planet isn't too anxious to share in the fate of Terron, so we really need to destroy the green robots' main server at any cost. It would also be highly desirable to get rid of the blazeroids and kelleroids as well.
50.RobotsWin: Clever! Who could have thought that beta-terronoids would go to such lengths to hide their server! Still, we knew such an old fox as this here ranger couldn't be easily snared. But what are we still doing here? Why don't we continue our discussion at the government building over a good cup of coffee?

51.GovTextLoss: Happy now? Don't even try to deny that you have received a transfer of <Money> cr from our competitors, apparently for some "covert operation." If we had a little more money, we would make sure you get to spend the rest of your days in solitary confinement. However, the Association of Mineral and Ore Exporters has already hired top notch shysters for you, so it makes little sense to incur the extra expense of going to court.
GovTextStart: Well, we do have a mission for you, but let me be brutally honest here: it isn't a walk in the park. However, you being a famous warrior and all that, we are sure you'd fit the bill nicely. You see, there is this huge volcanic sea on our planet, courtesy of seismic activities, which is also a bottomless source of valuable ores and rare earths. Basically, our planet's entire economy revolves around this huge pot of lava. We have hired the Galaxy's greatest minds to develop a high-tech automated mining complex for us that would be capable of operating under extremely high temperatures. Well, in hell, basically.

And now imagine -- the dominators decided they wanted this complex for themselves! At first we paid little attention to their landing party believing they would not be able to survive in these extreme temperatures. Later on, when we discovered the machines were equipped with special heat-proof armor, it was too late, and the facility was lost.
