It would be totally insane to send infantry or plasma tanks there, so the only option we have left is to hire a brave ranger such as yourself who would agree to control experimental heat-resistant robots.
51.GovTextWin: Great job, <Player>! It appears the chain of dominator-built plants is much more reliable and efficient than our own. The facility's output has increased by 150%, which, naturally, we are very happy about. On behalf of the government of planet <Planet>, it is my pleasure to present to you this modest check for <Money> cr -- about one percent of the enterprise's weekly profits.
51.Name: Combustion
51.RobotsLoss: This is a nightmare! Now it is even worse than it used to be! How could we entrust the fates of our planet to a character such as yourself? Very soon, the machines will begin building assault troops, so at this point we have no other recourse but to bomb the hell out of the facility.
RobotsStart: Commanding Ranger <Player>, requesting permission to report:

As kelleroids and blazeroids exhausted themselves fighting each other, we were able to capture the southern enrichment center. Once the dominators learned of our landing, they quickly proceeded to reinforce their positions, and now all their bases are virtually impregnable. The supreme command of the planet's armed forces recommends that you go on the defensive and begin accumulating the resources necessary for a subsequent assault on dominator-held bases. However, in view of our military's unsuccessful attempts to defend the planet, I would suggest you develop a more reliable plan.
RobotsWin: Great job, priv... I mean, Ranger <Player>. Dominator hulks will dissolve in the lava they have come out of and leave no traces. On the other hand, their production facilities will remain and contribute to our planet's industries nicely.
All you have left to do is get yourself a good sleep and give the government an after action report.

52.GovTextLoss: You have let us down so, <Player>! But since our planet participates in the loyalty program of the Ranger Center Network, your superiors will cover all our losses and even you will receive <Money> cr, which of course is nowhere near the amount you could have received had you completed your mission successfully. As to that island, while the Frozen Pussycats are licking their wounds and you mourn your miserly fee, we have declared general mobilization. Very soon, the island will be flooded with reservists who will blow the tin cans away. Still, keep it in mind that any fatalities among our soldiers will be on your conscience.
GovTextStart: Yes, Ranger <Player>, this is a job for you: we have problems with dominators, and what serious problems they are! These buggers landed on a tropical island and set up some sort of a production facility there that most likely involves cryogenic technology. The results were just horrible! Because of the rapid changes in local climate, the island began generating tropical hurricanes like there was no tomorrow. Coastal cities incurred serious damage and suffered great casualties. Ships continue to sink on the high seas regularly. Still, there is not much we can do since any strike from the orbit will cause the power plant located on the island to explode, which would in turn generate a giant tsunami and do even more harm to our cities.
You are our only hope, my dear ranger. Naturally, we'll be sure to pay you.
52.GovTextWin: Ah, <Player>! We are happy to see you again. What makes us even happier is that while you were on the way here our scientists managed to shut down that damn reactor, and the temperatures on the island are rising back to their hellish former selves that pose no climate challenges to us whatsoever. And you, I am sure you will be more than happy to learn that we have already transferred <Money> cr to your account.
52.Name: Cryo
52.RobotsLoss: What? Dominators are about to overrun our base? Board a flier ASAP. Third level, eighth door on the left. I said on the left! Phew, take off! The Ranger Center Network would have our hides if you died in an assault.
52.RobotsStart: You are finally here! Our Frozen Pussycats special forces detachment managed to get a toehold in a distant part of the island and even move further inland. However, the dominators detonated an electromagnetic bomb that sent us back to square one, even though the machines have not yet taken over all the production facilities. I suggest you hurry, <Player>. The enemy is strong and daring, and every hour we linger produces a new hurricane.
52.RobotsWin: Victory! The helicopter bringing in the scientists to shut down the reactor will arrive any minute now and pick you up on the way back. With this kind of cold, you could get frostbite easily.

53.GovTextLoss: Well, what do you want me to say, <Player>? To be sure, this was not a fair competition, but a contract is a contract, so the lion's share of the prize fund goes to the winner -- that is, not to you. What you will be getting is a modest amount of <Money> cr.
GovTextStart: How do you feel about the gaming industry, my good chap? You see, Clapon Co., a veteran of human gaming business, has come to our planet with a presentation of their new scripted shooter, Quarter-Life: Episode 451. As part of the celebration, they are organizing a tournament at a special range that will replicate one of the levels of their online game -- crossfire -- using modular robots for "players." But there's a wee bit of a problem: we couldn't find any qualified operators for this equipment. We did manage to connect two of the warring parties to captured dominator modules, but one role still remains up for grabs.
Yes, you guessed correctly: we suggest that you take on this role. And don't you worry, you will be pleasantly surprised by the prize money.
53.GovTextWin: Well, <Player>, I hope that you have had a chance to acquaint yourself with what Clapon folks are doing and give credit where it's due. What a wealth of options, secret hiding places sited for crossfire from different points, and all those "meat grinders" one had better avoid unless trained properly! We hope you will spend the <Money> cr you have won fair and square to continue your fight with the dominators, and for that reason the organizers are happy to give you a bonus... drum roll, please... A holocopy of the Quarter-Life: Episode 451, signed by the developers! Inside the case there is also a Quarter-Life badge with a unique serial number that you can wear next to your ranger badge to look more presentable.
53.Name: Crossfire
53.RobotsLoss: Is that right? Well, sure, breakdowns set us back, plus these two programmers, human and faeyan, did a heck of a job modifying textbook dominator behavior. Oh, and yes, there will be a flier picking you up to take you to the government building. I am afraid we are not going to have all that much room at the studio, and anyway the two major contestants to vie for most of the prize money will now be Cellanori and Mutnick.
RobotsStart: Um... we are sorry to inform you that we have had some difficulties getting your base connected. It now appears this will not be a fair fight since due to some serious oversight on the part of our technicians your base is going to be only half as effective at best as those of your opponents. On the other hand, we will make up for that by sending you regular reinforcements from the mainland.
And so-o-o-o-o, ladies and gentlemen!
THREE...
TWO...
ONE...
FIGHT!!!
RobotsWin: And the battle is now over, with Ranger <Player> winning a resounding victory over dominator teams. The spectator crowds are having a fit, and Messrs Mutnick and Cellanori that programmed the dominator bases are wringing their hands. Artificial intelligence proved to be no match for a live humanoid.
Any moment now flierzines will descend upon the grounds to bring our champion back to the studio in style.

54.GovTextLoss: Had you finished listening to the instructions and buckled up, you would have at least come out of this in one piece. My God, it hurts to even look at you, you are just one big bruise. Here's your <Money> cr, go see yourself a good doctor, or better yet buy a new powerful engine and leave this planet ASAP.
54.GovTextStart: A secret mission, you say? Well, it's hardly a secret anymore, but it sure is important. Oh, yes, it's not like you are following our news... We have us an emergency here. During a recent dominator attack, a small ship of theirs descended upon our planet and headed towards a fortified sea rig, apparently spoiling for a good fight. It's not like you could expect any different from a blazeroid. Were it a regular oil rig, we would have simply had the fleet blow it up, but this one here mines for a very rare mineral, neoninastin -- a powerful energy source, high-temperature superconductor and, most importantly, a valuable flora neonization catalyst. I hope you remember, ranger, that faeyans cannot digest food from other planets that has not been neonized. I am sure you'll be interested to know that faeyans pay millions of credits for a kilo of purified blue neoninastin gel. So it should go without saying now that we are not just going to simply give up on that money. We are going to fight and get the platform back, whatever the cost -- economically feasible cost, that is. We were about to send our special forces there, but then you descended upon us -- a godsent, seeing that you are a ranger licensed to operate combat robots. To be sure, robots cause a lot of damage on site, but you should see those maloq louts our soldier boys have recruited. You can trust them to burn the place to the ground, destroy everything and eat the debris, so if you agree to take on the task of clearing the platform we will be sure to pay you nicely for your troubles.
GovTextWin: Hold on a second... Could you please turn your right pocket inside out? Just so you'd know, there's an automatic gun turret behind you pointing down from the ceiling. Do not turn around. Do not make any sharp moves.

What's that, a pack of gum? Oh, sorry, our scanners took it for a box of neoninastin. All right, all right, don't hold it against me. Here, I think <Money> cr should make you feel better. Oh, and by the way, try not to gloat too much in the faces of the Red Hatchets waiting outside. They do not yet know you have taken their contract, but who knows, they may be intelligent enough to read that much on your happy face.
54.Name: Fuel for Life
54.RobotsLoss: I am afraid we cannot send a helicopter to pick you up from the rig while it is being besieged by blazeroids. You will have to use the rapid evacuation system. There's gotta be a red push button under protective cover somewhere next to your panel, but before you push it--
54.RobotsStart: I'll fire your damn butts, you elliptical idiots! Sorry, ranger, that wasn't for you, it's those faeyan technicians of ours who have just lost control of the platform's outer plants and let a blazeroid flier hook up to the storage at the loading dock. It means that the dominators have just gained themselves access to a huge resource cache, and it will make your mission all the more difficult. Let me suggest, if I may, that you deny the titanium plants to the enemy at all costs. That's what they were really short on at that dock, so the dominators will quickly exhaust whatever was available at that place -- that is, unless they take over the plants.
54.RobotsWin: That was really something, ranger! Explosions everywhere, rivers of napalm, plasma bursts and what not -- and the platform has barely a scratch on it! But enough about the platform. You are probably sick and tired of that tin can wide open to the winds, are you not? We are going to come and get you right away.

55.GovTextLoss: Poseidon took a shot, but the shield weakened the impact, and the underground laboratories remained unharmed. Even though you failed to accomplish the mission, you are being given a bonus of <Money> cr for your bravery. By the way, we are planning to mount an assault on the underground laboratories soon using faeyan digging machines, but we are not going to give this mission to you since you have proven yourself a very unreliable strategist.
GovTextStart: You want a job, ranger? Do you know how to keep your mouth shut? All right, then take a listen. 313 years ago to a day, a new type of a neutron weapon was tested on our planet that affected not only organic matter but klissan as well. The launch was to take place at the secret Station 82 pad, the target being an immobilized klissan egemon loitering high up in the atmosphere. However, 13 seconds into the flight the guidance system shorted, and the missile with a neutron warhead went out of control. As luck would have it, the missile fell on the very secret research station, City-113, where it had been developed. After the incident, all contact was lost with the base, and when we sent a rescue mission over to look for survivors their whirlybird disappeared without a trace while on approach. It was later discovered that some bespectacled eager beaver had managed to register an electromagnetic spike caused by the whirlybird's exploding generator. Naturally, the little prick spilled the beans to the press right away. Unsurprisingly, the island was immediately flooded by reporters believing City-113 to be a new Bermuda Triangle.

So, where was I? Ah! Quite recently, over three hundred years later, the cloud cover over the island and City-113 finally lifted, and orbital observation stations detected dominators there -- and of two different series models to boot. How they got there is a total mystery since there have been no machine invasions detected on our planet in recent history. Anyhow, all that fear-mongering by the damn scribblers has taken root, and now our land forces flat out refuse to deploy to the island. You are not superstitious, <Player>, are you? All we are asking of you is to lead our combat equipment on the island and do away with the dominator threat.
55.GovTextWin: Can you frigging imagine that? 13 seconds before the shot Poseidon's guidance system was hit by a meteorite! The gun scorched the entire surface of the island, but the underground facilities with their dangerous experimental stuff survived unharmed. Still, you accomplished your mission and deserve your <Money> cr. And while the Poseidon is being reloaded, we are looking for a ranger to mop up the underground facilities. Would you care to participate? Though in all fairness you must be tired. Get some rest.
55.Name: City-113
55.RobotsLoss: Dominators are about to overrun our base! No! I am too young to die! On second thought, no, get into the whirlybird, pronto! There's going to be enough room for the two of us. Let's get out of here!
55.RobotsStart: Excellent. There's been some good news from the island while we were in transit. It appears the dominators have gained access to the old research bunkers and used them to launch production of extra long-range chemical, biological and electromagnetic weapons. The island itself is polluted with chemical and radioactive waste, so it is of no use to us whatsoever. The Ministry of Defense made a decision to destroy the island using the Poseidon orbital gun. There is, however, one problem: the blazeroids unfurled an electromagnetic shield over the island. Once the Poseidon's ray overcomes the protective shield, it will have just enough oomph left in it to sterilize the surface, but not to penetrate the underground where most of the dominator forces will be sitting it out. With this in mind, your mission has changed somewhat to include weakening the protective shield somewhat. To that end, <clr>energy distributors<clrEnd> will need to be destroyed. They look like <clr>two columns running with white and blue waves<clrEnd>. These columns are very fragile at the base. Once you destroy both of those distributors, consider your mission accomplished. Try to do it all quickly, all right, <Player>? This damn place is giving me the creeps. What if it's all true -- all those ghost stories, disappearing ships and whatnot?
55.RobotsWin: The shield is lifting! Hurry up, <Player>, let's get back to the base. I saved you a place aboard my whirlybird. Hurry up! The sooner we report back, the sooner Poseidon will be able to take a shot.

56.GovTextLoss: Too bad we have these Galactic Council observers snooping around, or you would get yourself a taste of maloq vengeance. Moreover, these bas... observers are saying that you are owed compensation for having not fled from the battlefield. If you had fled, they would have brought you back here in a jar! What? Oh, yes, compensation. Here's some change -- <Money> cr -- just enough for a funeral, which would be in order if you don't get out of my sight quickly enough.
GovTextStart: I don't know about any coffee, but we do have a mission for you. And not just a mission -- a Mission with a capital M! In case you don't know, even before becoming a spacefaring race, we maloqs had fought plenty of wars with the aliens -- ancient gaals, karaps, etc. Some of our prisoners of war held on different planets managed to free themselves and even kick our enemies out of there since we procreate so much faster than all those alien sissies and fight so much better. This is exactly how our planet happened to come under maloq rule. We still have on display General Grubaxar's camp that he had set up near a karap pyramid that he would later blow to pieces with their very own guns. Oh, those were the days... Later on, we did restore the pyramid too, by the way, albeit without all those karap knickknacks. Still, you wouldn't be able to tell the difference just by looking at it. So, what was I talking about?

Oh yes, the dominators! You see, they decided to capture that legendary battlefield. And not that we'd mind them fighting each other a little, but they went about messing up Grubaxar's camp, and that's totally unacceptable. It is our national relic, for crying out loud! Long story short, ranger, if you are not a complete coward you simply have to help us liberate the camp, along with the entire historical complex while you are at it.
56.GovTextWin: Let me greet you warrior style, my friend! Hey, why are you covering your face? All right, let me just shake your brave hand then. It is fearless warriors such as yourself that uphold our Coalition. Oh yes, you are a ranger too, and all rangers need money. Well, we can't exactly pay you your weight in gold, but <Money> cr wouldn't be too shabby either, would it?
56.Name: Grubaxar
56.RobotsLoss: Oh me maloq mamma! The general would turn in his grave, had he not been timely cremated, if he knew a drab mediocrity such as yourself is now prowling the fields of his glory. But it's all right, a helicopter will come pick you up any time now, and then I guess I'll see you at your own court-martial, he-he.
56.RobotsStart: Long live General Grubaxar! Sorry, but this is an old tradition of ours -- to salute our nation's founding father when coming here. By the way, his camp is a bit to the south, and it's been taken over by blazeroids. To tell you the truth, the general's spirit wouldn't have put up with any other series of dominators, but I guess he is somehow all right with mechanical warriors. And the terronoids took over the replica of the karap pyramid, apparently for hope of maybe restarting some of the ancient machinery. What a bunch of idiots! Fortunately, there is nothing but steel and concrete there. So go ahead now, win your victory!
56.RobotsWin: Were there general alive today, he would shower you with kisses! What a will to win! What a push! Dominators didn't even have time enough to know what hit them! Now this place will have double the glory!

GovTextLoss: The sky is falling, <Player>! Because of your incompetence, this great ancient monument will be destroyed by some damn robots that have no sense of beauty and couldn't give a rat's batootie about the importance of history. You had all of our own robots destroyed in this senseless battle, and now all we have left to do is watch the dominators rip the island apart. Please, don't pour salt on my wound, if that's the right way to put it. Or maybe it's sugar. And no, sorry doesn't cut it.
Oh God, I can't even look into your sad puppy eyes. Here, take these <Money> cr as compensation for your time and leave me the heck alone.
GovTextStart: Ranger <Player>, we need your help.

We have this island on our planet with a unique monument harking back to some ancient events that no one even remembers anymore. However, the great granite slabs with names on them had survived through the times and still guard some kind of a secret that we have not been able to learn yet. The only thing that we do know is that there are some mysterious caves under the monument, and that every once in a while it sends strange signals into space that no one can decipher. Archaeologists of all races keep asking me for permission to do a complete study and dig the place up, but I cannot be responsible for anything that may result in this great monument's destruction since every year it attracts hundreds of thousands of tourists and pilgrims. To be sure, some folks at the SNK transplanetary corporation know something about the memorial, but they are never going to tell, may they be damned along with their corporate ethics.

Anyhow, <Player>, everything would have been hunky-dory had it not been for dominators that descended upon that blessed island a few days ago. Apparently, they were lured in by those mysterious signals. What's really exasperating is that they could destroy the great monument without ever asking me -- and that pisses me off! We must kick them off the island ASAP before they mess the monument beyond any recognition. I do not want to go down in history as the ruler on whose watch the great monument was destroyed, so I am prepared to pay you <Money> cr if your mission is successful.
GovTextWin: <Player>, you did it! I was watching the battle through an orbital station and I must tell you it is truly a great victory! You are a strategic genius, and no, no, don't wave me off! You deserve full credit here. And <Money> cr, of course. Once again, congratulations on your victory! And let me promise you that when we finally solve the mystery of this monument I will write to you and tell you all about it.
And now, if you would excuse me, I need to go concern myself with preventing any future dominator attacks on the island.
57.Name: In Memoriam
57.RobotsLoss: Ranger, you botched this battle completely! Just scram before they send you to meet your maker, like they did with your busted robots. We suggest you report to the government building to be properly yelled at.
57.RobotsStart: Ranger, all your initial resources are ready, so you can go into battle now. Only first sign this obligation to do as little damage as possible to the island and everything on it. If you start blasting away indiscriminately and damage something, we will shoot you ourselves. Any questions? In this case don't drag your feet and go straight into battle.
57.RobotsWin: Great, you did it! Dominators have been destroyed, and the monument is safe! Have yourself some R&R now, take time to explore the island and then report to the government building to claim your well-deserved reward.

58.GovTextLoss: Call Boris Willis immediately! I know he specializes in asteroids, but this is as close as it gets. What, you are still here? Waiting to get compensated, no less, huh? Oh, you sure do know lost battles have to be paid for as well. Smart guy! Here! Here's you <Money< cr, you louse! Now get out of my sight!
GovTextStart: What mission? Don't you see I am having a panic attack? Aaaah! We are all gonna die! All right, all right: breathe in, breathe out... No, we are doomed! Aaaah! One second, hello! Yeah, there is this one guy.

Ranger, you have been afforded a great honor -- to save our planet's capital from nuclear doom. What do you mean, "how much"? What happened to honor? That's just not right... Anyhow, here's the island, and here are the dominators, and an Apocalypse class nuclear ICBM, and a launcher... In a few hours they will shoot it at our lovely capital, and the thing's got enough oomph in it to launch the entire city into orbit. There's no time to lose. We have no toehold on the island at all, and the ranger before you lost the base. And the damn clock is ticking. I am not going to feed you the entire line. Here's a contract, you can sign it or otherwise simply remove yourself to another spaceport. I am on my way to get my family into a bunker.
We are all gonna die!
58.GovTextWin: You are our savior, <Player>! I don't even know how we could ever pay our debt to you... How much?... Are you out of your mind? The most we could afford would be <Money> cr. You know, assault operations and evacuations are not exactly cheap these days. We have a deal? Then please sign this receipt.
58.RobotsLoss: Aah! We are all gonna die! Repent, you sinners, because time has come... And why are you not repenting? You think they'll send a helicopter for you? Unfortunately, you are right, even though I would leave your bones to rot right here on this island if it were up to me.
58.RobotsStart: The situation couldn't possibly be any worse. Those air force idiots dropped the robots and self-unpacking turrets amidst the ruins of an old fortress. The flier with the mobile base aboard was shot down on approach, and the bomber that was sent to blow up the terronoid base had been loaded with mines rather than bombs by mistake. How can you possibly trust the military after something like this? Do what you can. The fortress, even though it is all in ruins and overgrown with the jungle in places, may still help you fend off the assault. We managed to squeeze the military for another assault force, but they need a factory-made beacon to land at the right spot. You may also want to know that the unexploded mines sitting in craters around the terronoid base may still be detonated if hit with regular guns, and the kelleroid base that the "green" series used to control still has a number of robot generators and nuclear fuel tanks in storage. If you manage to activate the generators, you could then provoke a fight in the immediate vicinity of unexploded ordnance.
58.RobotsWin: We are saved! While you were fighting here, our capital has been evacuated. It's not that we didn't trust your talents, but we still prepared ourselves for the worst. A helicopter will take you to the bunker zone space port -- that's where all the government has been sequestered -- and engineering teams will then arrive at the island to dismantle the missile.

59.GovTextLoss: Don't you fret about it so, our crisis center was insured. As per your your standard strategist contract, you are getting <Money> cr. Regardless, it is very unlikely we will ever offer you another job.
59.GovTextStart: You know, <Player>, these days many governments make advance preparations for fending off dominator invasions. Thus, gaals and faeyans develop planetary shields, maloqs build underground shelters for their entire populations, and pelengs have arrangements in place for urgent evacuation of the government and the state treasury. As for us, we have developed an automatic crisis center that will wage asymmetric warfare once our planet is taken over by dominators, so as to speed up its future liberation. But by a stroke of bad luck dominators landed right on the secret island where the crisis center is located. And believe it or not, they are none the wiser to what powerful weapon they now have in their possession. As it happens, they have been attracted by a titanium deposit. Moreover, the kelleroids that took over the air defense center have already shot down half a dozen other rangers we sent on rescue missions, so we cannot guarantee your personal safety. So, are you going to take it or should we keep looking for someone who has more guts?
59.GovTextWin: Sign here, please. This is a non-disclosure agreement with respect to any government secrets you may learn. The crisis center was built without an approval by the Galactic Council. And now sign here. This is a receipt for <Money> cr that has already been transferred to your account. We will aways be glad to see you on our planet.
59.Name: Crisis Center
59.RobotsLoss: That's all right, our analysts have estimated your chances of success at 15% at the utmost, so it's not like we expected anything better. A helicopter will come pick you up any minute now, and the island will self-destruct in three hours.
59.RobotsStart: Yes, this new stealth flier model did manage to fool the enemy's air defenses. That is, our very own air defenses now used by the enemy. All right, <Player>, let me give you a rundown of the situation. You have at your disposal a great fortified command center hidden from casual observers inside a mountain of ice. Kelleroids that pose the biggest threat have dug in at the air defense facilities while blazeroids took over the chemical weapons storage in the extreme south. Right before your arrival, a kelleroid submarine delivered a brigade of assault troops to the secret port. Your primary task is to clear the crisis center of dominators. To achieve your objective, you will be able to use hidden nuclear charges planted near the locations dominators have used to set up their bases and in a number of other places.
59.RobotsWin: Victory! Don't you sense the intoxicating aroma of this very word? We finally have the crisis center back under our control, and it is unlikely to ever be captured again.

60.GovTextLoss: Were you a member of the brotherhood, you would now have to answer to the Prophet, but you are just a mercenary, and the brotherhood doesn't want any blots on its good name. You will receive <Money> cr as standard compensation, but if I were you I wouldn't expect to get any more work from us.
60.GovTextStart: Even after our planet was liberated, a fraction of the dominator land force refused to put down their arms, and at the moment hostilities are still ongoing in many areas between what's left of them and KVSMK assault troops. Still, certain areas with no strategic importance have been abandoned, and as it happens one of them is home to the Bove Brotherhood shrine and the underground Scorpion Temple where Prophet Caain blessed his followers before the victorious war with the union of infidels that would not bow to the power of the Unguided Killerator. Today, this patch of sacred land that in the course of history has become an island, is being held by dominators. Unfortunately, KVSMK generals wouldn't even let us have a mobile base, but if you feel you could defeat a superior force of machines we would give you a brigade of assault troops to command. Naturally, you should also consider the potential reward that on top of the undying respect from all the Brothers would also include a substantial amount of money -- <Money> credits.
60.GovTextWin: <Player>, I don't think you can even fathom how important it is for us to win. Sure, let the soldier boys protect our cities and plants, but what kind of people would we be if we let the enemy raze our temple -- the very place from where the Prophet had led us to victory, where he was murdered three times and where he gave us His covenants. What do you mean he couldn't have been murdered three times? He was a Prophet, ranger, not a mere mortal. Still, a rare alien is capable of understanding the Bove religion, and you are hardly an exception. Be it as it may, you have earned your fee of <Money> cr in good faith, and the brothers will always be happy to see you again on our planet.
60.Name: Triple Blow
60.RobotsLoss: The temple has been destroyed a number of times before, but back then those were strong and resolute opponents. What we are facing today is a minuscule force of machines fighting each other, and we are just not going to stand by and watch them desecrate our holy place. I am at a loss for words to express my feelings, but I am sure that once you are brought to the government building proper words will be found, to be followed by appropriate action.
60.RobotsStart: The Prophet has never advocated procrastination and apathy, and I suggest you hark to His ultimate wisdom, <Player>. Your enemies are as powerful as they are numerous, but at the moment, before they are ready to launch an attack, you could still take advantage of your superior firepower and mobility. Take quick and decisive action, ranger. For the glory of the Brotherhood!
60.RobotsWin: Caain Lives On!!! Verily, it is the holy day today, and the temple is flowing with the bloo... the engine oil of the Prophet's enemies. Representatives from the fifth colum... I mean, the government are waiting to decorate you.

61.GovTextLoss: And there's our hero! A round of applause for the hero, please! He did not chicken out in the face of danger and stood his ground to the last, even when there was no more hope left, for which he deserves a consolation prize of <Money> cr. This is where we say goodbye to our participant, and we will see you, our dear stereoviewers, next week on the next episode of the Classic Epic Battles of Combat Robots in Fantasy Worlds.
GovTextStart: Ranger <Player>, have you ever heard of the roleplaying society? They are very interesting humans and gaals with keen imaginations and deep pockets. Some thirty years ago, one of those groups put together enough money to reenact a certain battle between imaginary peoples in an imaginary world. The script was written by some ancient human professor. I must admit that that creation of theirs became one of our planet's wonders and gave rise to a decent tourist business in between the reenacted battles. But as you may have already guessed all of it went down the drain when dominators descended upon us.

Naturally, the Galactic Endorist-Ardist Society demands that we take decisive action. At the same time, they insist that we preserve the fortresses built on the battlefield, for which reason our only reliable option here would be using modular robots. I was informed by the authorities that you are fully licensed to operate those. And believe me, you will need every ounce of your skills here since many a ranger has already singed his wings trying to crack this mission. Yes, our enemies are that strong.
GovTextWin: Congratulations, <Player>! You won! And not just won -- you beat the record too! No one before you could ever take all the three fortresses in less than twenty-four hours. By the way, smile -- you have been filmed by hidden cameras. Oh, come on, don't be a grump! You are a celebrity now, especially among the roleplaying society that makes up most of the regular audience for our Classic Epic Battles of Combat Robots in Fantasy Worlds. Not only did you get more famous -- you are now richer as well. To the tune of <Money> cr.

And... You know what, when we have our new proving grounds ready we will make sure to invite you again, only maybe without all this masquerade. Err... go do what? My, we had no idea you were so grouchy!
61.Name: Siege
61.RobotsLoss: You did fairly good, <Player>, good enough for the bet I made on you. Don't despair. You see, I may have made a thousand credits here, but you are not going to be left high and dry either. Better go back to the stu... government building. They are going to explain everything to you there.
61.RobotsStart: You are finally here! You know, it is kind of funny that you will be commanding the Monas Terry fortress that is a bastion of good in that professor's original opus. The evil fortresses, whatever their names are, I don't quite remember, have been occupied by kelleroids and blazeroids, and despite their proximity to each other they are regularly exhibiting an inordinate interest in our positions. However, your first target would be the poorly fortified terronoid camp in the immediate vicinity of your Terry.
61.RobotsWin: What a spectacle! Take my professional word for it: there's enough material here for a few seasons, and... Why are you looking at me this way? Oh, yes, you don't know... Then I am not going to spoil the surprise.

62.GovTextLoss: What a pity! What a great, great pity! Alas, the pyramid has been lost, and now we will never learn the secret of the karap civilization. Naturally, it's not like we are blaming you for that. It was a very complicated battle, and we should have simply tapped a better strategist. Nevertheless, you have showed great courage defending your base to the very end. Our Indy Jokes, who on top of being an archaeologist is also a famous adventurer and daredevil, was so impressed that he decided to pay you <Money> cr out of his own personal savings as a sign of his deep appreciation for your efforts.
62.GovTextStart: Oh, Ranger <Player>! Your timing couldn't be better -- dominators have taken over the dig site and are now threatening to destroy the pyramid. Wait, haven't you heard? That was a discovery of the century! Doctor Indy Jokes, a famous archaeologist, found and dug up the first ever operational karap pyramid. Don't tell me you never heard of the karaps! To make it real simple for a person of your erudition, the karaps were a very advanced ancient race that disappeared without a trace some three and a half thousand years ago leaving behind multiple high-technology artifacts all over the galaxy. There are reasons to believe that they disappeared after a war with ancient gaals, but the gaals themselves flat our refuse to share such "shameful episodes of our history" with the rest of us. Until recently, studying the karap civilization was all the more difficult since they left no writings and stored all information on digital media that are notorious for their poor durability. But then an expedition led by Doctor Jokes found an entire operational pyramid, intact with all its archives. Unfortunately, they have also unearthed a secret underground dominator base and had to retreat under cover of a rearguard action. The worst of it was that blazeroids whose base was destroyed during the dig set up camp on top of the pyramid and began transforming it to their own liking. I hope you understand that we cannot use orbital guns or nuclear weapons since the Galactic Council has already designated the pyramid a monument of universal importance, and we will face huge sanctions if it is lost. Fortunately, we had a mobile, self-unpacking base available that we managed to drop from the air in the vicinity of the dig site. Now all we need to do is find a strategist. Your file says that you have been trained for exactly this kind of missions, so, as the saying goes, more power to you.
62.GovTextWin: Oh, it's you, ranger. Sorry I yelled at you. It was only later that we found that the damage sustained by the pyramid was cosmetic, and the internal machinery survived intact. By the way, Doctor Jokes has already begun deciphering the ancient writings, which in itself is very encouraging. And I bet <Money> cr we will pay you for the mission so brilliantly accomplished will be sure to lift your own spirits.
62.Name: Pyramid
62.RobotsLoss: A-a-a! They will fire my butt! No, they'll put me in front of a firing squad! Or worse yet, send me with Jokes on another uguptian expedition. It is all your fault, <Player>! How could you lose so stupidly?
62.RobotsStart: Great! I knew you would do it! You will only have a base and a couple of plants at your disposal for the time being, but judging by your record you have seen worse. As you can see, blazeroids have dug in real well on the slopes of the pyramid and are likely to be using its resources. Terronoids are restricted to their own base for now, but soon enough they will want to expand. I am not sure what to recommend at this point. Some analysts suggest you sic the dominators on each other, others that you storm the underground bunkers and yet others that you dislodge the blazeroids from the pyramid. But it's your call!
62.RobotsWin: What a mess! What a nightmare! This is totally unacceptable! Yes, I am fully aware that you won the battle, but why on earth did you have to smash this priceless archaeological relic? Report to the government building immediately, they will teach you a little respect for history there!

63.GovTextLoss: It would serve you right if we threw you in jail for a couple of years, but there is this damn contract... Now the gaals will strangle us with their sanctions for selling drugs, and the pelengs will impose an embargo, if not an outright trade blockade, for competing with them. And I will be sure to get fired. Are you gloating, ranger? Go ahead, gloat, but don't ever expect us to give you another job. We wouldn't even pay you the <Money> cr were it not in the contract.
63.GovTextStart: Say, <Player>, have you ever heard the name of Olmian Cellanori? No? How about Dazykagz Sisha? Oh, now I see your eyes lighting up! And by the way, why do they shine in such a suspicious manner? Oh, anyway. You are probably aware that Dazykagz heads a large peleng drug cartel, the Sleazy Hands, and Olmian is a famous computer programmer, inventor and hacker wanted in 10 different systems. By the way, it was Cellanori who in the year 3299 found a way to manufacture and reprogram modular dominator robots that now make up the backbone of our land forces. Now he has begun using these robots against us. But let's get back to the business at hand. Our planet's western oceanic hemisphere has seen a recent rise of electromagnetic activity, which is very suspicious considering the area is not populated. Besides, the gaals began complaining about our planet allegedly exporting drugs. All of this called for a serious investigation that discovered an island plantation of opium poppies -- a source of elite natural drugs. Subsequent observations confirmed that it was a partnership venture by Sisha and Cellanori who also built a low-orbit flier port and a refining lab at the plantation. The island is protected by solid air defenses and a troop of reprogrammed dominator robots. The SWAT teams we have sent were easily repelled by kelleroids, so that Cellanori did not even have to tap the terronoids he used to harvest the crops. We were about to send the SQUAT special forces in, but here comes you -- an experienced strategist. Everyone knows that the best way to fight modular robots is with modular robots of your own. We are ready to offer you a standard freelance strategist contract and pay you handsomely. Say yes.
63.GovTextWin: Wake up, <Player>! I see you've had yourself a lungful too many of narcotic fumes. All right, all right, quit that kissing business! I don't want to be dragged to court over this. Your success on the battlefield hasn't been in vain. The SQUAT team used the portal to reach the Sleazy Hands' headquarters and arrest everyone who didn't flee, including Dazykagz Sisha. We couldn't get Cellanori, but one way or another we have restored our planet's reputation and even improved it a bit while you got a little richer too -- to the tune of <Money> cr.
63.Name: Plan
63.RobotsLoss: How could you lose? Do you even understand that this base could well flood entire sectors with drugs derailing the lives of billions of humanoids and, most importantly, destroying our trade with the gaals and the pelengs? You don't understand it? That's all right, they'll set you straight at the government building.
63.RobotsStart: Oh, there you are at last, ranger! As you can see, our previous operations have only gotten us this little toehold that we were able to hold on to, albeit just barely, until you arrived. The spread of new manufacturing plants has been curbed somewhat after our strike aircraft dropped electromagnetic bombs on the island. But considering the losses sustained, we are not going to send another wave in. As you may have noticed, the terronoids that were used to harvest the crops and transport them to a storage location have mostly been destroyed. However, their bases are still capable of cranking out plenty of new robots. The kelleroids that were primarily used to provide technical support to the processing facilities have also begun building an army. It could have been even worse had our SWAT experts not been able to plant a virus removing the combat tolerance marker from these robots' operating software. This means our opponents will go at each other's throats first. Your mission remains unchanged -- to destroy the enemy. Get on with it.
63.RobotsWin: What a grand battle! What a glorious victory! What's this otherworldly... ...smell? What is it, <Player>? The poppy fields are burning? Oh, I don't know... Ha-ha-ha. What can I tell you? I love you so much, <Player>! Those lovely spheres! Do you see them? I am so happy, and you will be happy too when you get to the government building.

64.GovTextLoss: The situation is critical. The battleship has sailed and our fleet is racing to intercept it. The situation is aggravated by a terrible storm that has already disabled cruiser Chicagov and sunk destroyer Vagary. If the weather deteriorates even further, our fleet will never be able to rendezvous with Alexei Potyomker Stauridian. Naturally, we are not going to blame you for that since the battle was very difficult, and very few experienced strategists would have been able to last as long as you had. Unfortunately, due to the extra expense of having to pay compensation to the families of Vagary's lost crew, we will not be able to pay you the amount promised. <Money> cr, that's all you will be getting. Please don't hold it against us.
64.GovTextStart: Hello, Ranger <Player>. It's quite handy that you dropped in. At the moment, not only the Escallop National Park alone is threatened to be destroyed, but also the rich cities on the Louter Banks, of which this particular island is part of. You've never heard of the Escallop, is that what you are saying? OK, since you are not local, let me explain. This is about the only untouched stretch of wilderness on planet <Planet> most of which has by now been densely developed. It has been spared development not only because it is protected by the government but also in view of its powerful seismic activity. Almost every year the island is rattled by powerful quakes, and massive eruptions happen a few times a century. Dominators must have been unaware of that, or they wouldn't have built their base in such a dangerous place. Were it any other location, we wouldn't hesitate to bombard it from the orbit. However, in this case Greenpeace would have the shirt off our backs for destroying the Escallop, and, second, the island is surrounded with a powerful barrier shield that could protect it from such a bombardment and interfere with our scanners. Whatever bits of information we do have indicate that the dominators are preparing a seaborne assault and are almost ready to sail. It will take us a while to put together naval assets sufficient for an intercept, so in order to buy time we need an experienced strategist such as yourself. A heavy combat flier carrier is already standing by.
64.GovTextWin: Oh, that's you, <Player>! Here is your <Money> cr. Now go. I said go, I can't deal with you right now. Battleship Potyomker is giving us trouble again. A landing party hiding in the cargo bay mounted an assault and suppressed whatever resistance our own troops managed to offer. The ship has sailed, apparently to the Louter Banks. Despite a bad storm, our own navy is going full steam ahead to intercept, and the outcome of this operation now depends on our sailors. So what do you want? You are a ranger, not a sailor, so we don't need your services any longer.
64.Name: Escallop
64.RobotsLoss: Quod erat demonstrandum. The situation couldn't possibly be worse. I am not even sure I should tell you. We had to abandon our blocking position because of the storm, and Potyomker now has smooth sailing all the way to the Louter Banks. Anyway, you've done all you could, and I am in no position to blame you. Use the teleportation module on your flier for emergency evacuation.
64.RobotsStart: The flier itself did a great job destroying blazeroid coastal defenses, but unfortunately its navigation system sustained serious damage in the process, and it is unlikely to ever take off again. Now, a quick brief. Terronoids that have previously been badly battered by blazeroid troops dug in inside the crater of the volcano. However, with the coastal base gone now, they are much more of a threat. As to the blazeroids, during their occupation they have rebuilt and restored the battleship Prince Alexei Potyomker Stauridian sunk in the Old Blazeful's caldera, turning that pile of old scrap into a powerful ship equipped with a barrier shield generator. At the moment, the situation is quite dire. Your opponents are strong and hold strategically more favorable positions, so we are not going to blame you if you lose. The important part is to buy us some time until the fleet arrives.
64.RobotsWin: Outstanding! To be honest with you, we never expected you to be so successful and prepared for the worst since the island blockade had to be lifted because of the Category 11 storm. Had you lost, the blazeroids could have easily landed on the beaches of our coastal cities. Now this threat has been eliminated and you can report to the mainland to claim your reward.

65.GovTextLoss: You are black and blue all over, <Player>! You should have finished listening to the instructions, buckled up and put on your helmet. It's all your fault, and it's your fault too that you lost. Now we'll need to start the attack from scratch again, but at least we've already found your replacement. In all fairness though, the stereovision folks that made a bundle broadcasting the fight will pay you <Money> cr as a royalty, but believe me, this is nothing like what you could have received if you won.
65.GovTextStart: Oh, yes, we have a mission for you, and a fairly difficult one too. One of our planet's moons has vast oceans of molten heavy hydrocarbons that are being mined by the human company Snell. However, not too long ago one of their most profitable rigs was attacked by dominators who started rearranging it for their own needs that we suspect include building a storm troop of combat robots. Naturally, we could just bomb the facility built by the machines right out of the heavy bitumen it is floating on, but Snell's lawyers have already warned us they will have the shirts off our backs if we do. Thus, our only option is to send over a ranger -- and that would be you -- to command combat robots. I hope you are good at strategy. Are you?
65.GovTextWin: Bravo, <Player>! Bravo! I particularly liked the part where the blazeroid column stormed the base held by Keller's robots. Even though I have to admit your own fights were fairly graphic too. By the way, your fee will be increased by the amount of stereovision royalties and a bonus from Snell, so it comes down to a fairly nice chunk of cash -- <Money> cr.
65.Name: Red Alert
65.RobotsLoss: Defect at once! No, deject-- Oh, no, eject, that's what I meant! You have an escape pod built into your base. Just push the big red button, and you will be ej--
65.RobotsStart: I think it's time to let you know that you are not the first to give this job a crack. You predecessor is now on the way to the planet to be treated for nerve gas poisoning after leading an attack on the terronoids that we have now captured and made our very own. Fortunately, neither of the two remaining series has this chemical weapon on hand, so it is all up to you.
65.RobotsWin: That was a magnificent victory, <Player>! The battle was broadcast over planetary stereovision channels, and the ratings were off the charts. Your fans -- and your fee -- are awaiting you on the mother planet.

66.GovTextLoss: Now tell me, <Player>, why don't you rangers ever bother to listen to instructions in their entirety? Because if you did buckle up, you would have gotten off with a mere scare. Well, anyway, while the armada is urgently repairing the damaged landing craft and reanimates the "long noses," we have enough time to prepare our defenses. What is particularly encouraging is that no Ryan is going to throw a monkey wrench into our plans -- and we mostly have you to thank for that. Of course, had you managed to stop the invasion army your reward would have been so much larger, but <Money> cr isn't small change either.
GovTextStart: You know, <Player>, not too long ago dominators tried to take over our system. Or maybe you don't know -- you rangers often stay out there in space for months, away from all the news. One way or another, we had blazeroids landing on our planet, with everything you would expect such a thing to entail: evacuations, Coalition storm troops arriving, the state of emergency being declared and panic breaking out. Still, even under such hectic circumstances the customs did a great job and figured out that there was a tiny discrepancy between those coming back and those that left or got killed in action. Namely, a certain John Anson Ryan was missing -- a native of Orlenon, a private in the plasma tanks and veteran of the first battle of Gralgar. You may not think it important, but there is nothing unimportant in security, so our security services took a look.

And they found him. Boy, did they really! Our private Ryan turned out to be no Ryan at all. Not a native of Orlenon, and not even human, but rather a terminator -- a blazeroid saboteur! While we were getting life back to normal and restoring order after the dominator attack, that bugger bought tons of different stuff on the black market and used it to assemble some primitive engineering bots and ore miners. In turn, those assembled more advanced specimen that then went to build an entire army of modular robots -- heavy assault droids, yes -- and a fairly large fleet to boot. All it took was a month and a half! Luckily, in order to keep his extracurricular activities quiet, "Ryan" built his army away from civilization, on an uninhabited island. And now this entire armada is heading towards our capital's metropolitan area, and the only thing in between them and us... well, there was this navy of ours and the air force, but the dominators did away with those even though it cost them dearly. Now the only defense our capital's harbor has is a well fortified island smack in the middle of the estuary. Our regular combat robot operator has been badly wounded and is now in intensive care. You are our last hope. Well, you and the ground forces that will fight the enemy on the beaches if it comes to that. Think long and hard -- we are talking about the lives of our soldiers here.
66.GovTextWin: On behalf of planet <Planet>, let me thank you profoundly. Not only have you spared our planet the horrors of war, but you also saved the lives of many of our soldiers. They have already begun synthesizing your statue for our pantheon of eternal glory even though I don't think you care much about such things -- you being a space vagabond and all that. Still, I believe <Money> cr that I am sure you will spend on your upcoming new battles with the machines will make for an attractive enough reward.
66.Name: Private Ryan
66.RobotsLoss: I am not going to pretend that we expected anything better once we saw what short work the blazeroid landing party made of our coastal base's layered defenses. We immediately began building additional defenses in the harbor itself. I recommend that you evacuate the base immediately. If you haven't noticed it yet, there is a covered button there labeled "eject." Just take a hammer and--
RobotsStart: While you were on the the way here, the situation deteriorated somewhat. Ryan, flying his personal armored helicopter and impervious to flak, captured the port and our air defenses. He then turned off the ammunition supply to our coastal batteries. The guns fired a salvo and then fell silent. Oh, the gloom! Our helicopters that were delivering storm troops to key defense points got shot down immediately. The terminator was unable to take over our island defenses, but we no longer control them either. In the meantime, the armada's landing craft went ashore, and the heavy "long nose" assault droids joined in. The situation would have become critical had it not been for the tesla-gun batteries we had waiting for them ashore and aboard your boat. However, before we zapped them with electric charges the heavy droids managed to do a lot of damage. Luckily, you were safely tucked away down below, in the cargo bay, so you couldn't see the bow of your boat being sliced right off.

Let me reiterate it: the situation is dire and our analysts that have planned the island's defenses are now pulling their hair out since all those plans got sabotaged. On a personal note, let me only add one thing: whack that damn terminator ASAP while he is still all alone in the port.
66.RobotsWin: Incredible! You know, we were getting ready to evacuate you and went about building defense positions around the harbor once we realized how dire the situation was. Helicopters will be arriving soon to bring in construction specialists to restore the battered defenses and take a look at those "long noses." You will be brought back to the capital that you have saved -- and this is no exaggeration.

67.GovTextLoss: Who did this to you -- dominators? Sailors, you say? Well, yeah, the vice admiral is known for his short temper. Nevertheless, after the assault troops were destroyed and the terronoids landed, our chances to win dwindled almost to zero. Still, after an attack by one of the terronoid mechanism's tentacles damaged the shield generator and U-2 was evacuated, orbital bombing vaporized all the ships and the octopus. Victory was won, but you were not the one who won it. Still, you are due a small compensation in the amount of <Money> cr. And now take your leave of us.
GovTextStart: Mission, <Player>? How are your sea legs? You see, we have a mission for a strategist capable of performing in confined spaces.

Our navy met a serious opponent: a sunk battleship restored by blazeroids came out of nowhere and easily destroyed two squadrons we have sent to intercept it. Then its boarding party captured our aircraft carrier, the Aurora. Still, before going down, our cruiser Storm managed to fire a cryogun salvo at the battleship and put its engines out of commission. We have put together a few hundreds of combat robots and landing craft for a boarding operation to get the Aurora back and liquidate the blazeroid threat. At the moment, we are looking for a suitable strategist.
If you agree -- and I am sure you will -- we will bring you aboard the U-2 submarine via teleporter, so that you could safely command the operation.
67.GovTextWin: You know, ranger, when the terronoid mechanism engaged we lost all hope this would somehow turn out well. Our only hope was that the terronoids would be able to damage or destroy the battleship before it defrosts. Despite all that, your tactical genius helped you win. Your heroism has been invaluable, but due to our outsized defense expenditures we will only be able to pay you <Money> cr. Here, please sign this receipt.
67.Name: Battleship
67.RobotsLoss: Four thousand devils down your throat! Petty officer, eject the base to be raised! Slow astern! Left nine degrees rudder! Five degrees down bubble! And you, ranger, are expected at the government building. Seaman, throw this landlubber into the teleporter!
RobotsStart: Open the flood valves! Flood torpedo tubes! Main caliber, battle stations! A civilian? A ranger? What are you doing aboard an attack submarine? Who gave you access to the teleporter? What kind of papers are those? Urgent orders? Give them to me! Aha... One moment... Hrm... Them damn landlubbers! Sorry, Commander <Player>, requesting permission to report! Hold on a sec! Close flood valves! Drain torpedo tubes! Yellow alert! Five degrees up bubble, left seven degrees rudder! All right, ranger, we will moor alongside the Aurora any minute now. The elevators will bring your base up, and you will go into battle. Landing craft are packed with robots, use them to blow the enemy away. Hold on a sec!

Ranger, we have a new development here! As soon as the craft moored alongside, the battleship fired a precise salvo and blew away the landing party. After that, what surfaced from the depths... What surfaced... You'll see for yourself what I am talking about! Now you only have your base left at your disposal, that and a couple of plants that with no troops to protect them will be captured by terronoids right away. Terronoids? What terronoids? You'll see for yourself soon. Good luck to you!
67.RobotsWin: What a magnificent operation! What a great victory! A crew of scientists and technicians have already left the mainland to study this unusual terronoid... structure. You are expected at the government building with your report.

68.GovTextLoss: Yes, it wasn't an easy mission, and you fought to the very end, but still you lost. Now this will be handled by faeyan mercenaries in exoskeleton suits, and they do not work cheap. Still, you are going to get some hazard money -- <Money> cr. -- since you have had to operate in the vicinity of a powerful source of electromagnetic radiation.
GovTextStart: Not too long ago, our planet barely escaped being hit by a very strange meteorite. Yes, barely, since it stopped dead in its tracks a few yards above the ground and antigravitated like there was no tomorrow. Moreover, this object that ignorant media scribblers have already dubbed as "Sphere", generates gigawatts of direct currents and shoots lightning all around - all the while maintaining the temperature of its surface constant at the water boiling point at local pressure. Many scientists would like to know what that wonder "Sphere" is and where it gets those vast quantities of energy necessary for antigravitation and other mayhem from. I'll tell you more, the fae have already offered us an exorbitant amount for the exclusive rights to conduct a study of this phenomenon.

But as you may have already guessed, the biggest problem was caused by dominators. Kelleroids picked up on this anomaly almost immediately and landed an assault troop, which in turn drew the attention of the other two series. Our special forces managed to handle the blazeroids all by themselves, but from this point on modular robots will be required, which you, if your file is accurate, are quite good with.
68.GovTextWin: Please forgive us, <Player>. We have already loaded a case of antiradiation pills into your ship. Take them three times daily after meals. By the way, the fae arrived in the middle of your battle, right on time for watching the endgame. You'll be pleased to know that they paid us <clr>1,000,000,000<clrEnd> credits for their exclusive rights. I don't think this money pot will suffer much if we pay you <Money> cr for a mission well accomplished.
68.Name: Sphere
68.RobotsLoss: Well, we have been expecting something of the kind. Plan Z will now get activated, so you'd be better off getting the hell out of here since the mercenaries have been ordered to destroy any structure captured by dominators.
68.RobotsStart: Congratulations on your soft landing, ranger. We kind of forgot to let you know that the Sphere jams navigation systems on all our fliers. By the way, when the dominators were landing, they lost many of their own as well. Fortunately, the inactive base that used to belong to blazeroids is located in the immediate vicinity of your landing site, even though one of the robots has exited the flier on the wrong side. Naturally, it is a different matter altogether that the flier blocked a strategic highway, and now the action plan developed by our analysts is only good for recycling. Use your own best judgment.
68.RobotsWin: The island has been fully cleared. Return to the mainland immediately before radiation does you in altogether. Didn't we warn you that the Sphere generates strong neutron and gamma ray background radiation?

69.GovTextLoss: General state of emergency on the planet, 30% of the population evacuated, antidote injections administered wholesale -- eew, yuck! -- and distribution of gas masks -- such are the effects of that poisonous cyanide cloud from the Zenith bombardment. Imagine how much better it would have been had you not lost! Still, there are some that do not view your actions as reprehensible at all. Religious fanatics from The End is Now society got really excited about your attempt to destroy life on this planet and even raised <Money> cr for you. Happy now? The official reward we put together for you would have been much larger. And now be so kind as to relieve us of your presence.
GovTextStart: Well, <Player>, we happen to have a job for you. It involves commanding robots under extreme conditions. Oh! I see your eyes lighting up already!

As you may know, our planet rotates around itself at the same speed as around its star. Since our orbital eccentricity is slightly above zero, one half of the planet is incessantly baked by the never-setting sun while the other is always dark and frozen solid. Naturally, all of our cities are located in the twilight zone that offers moderate temperatures. However, in the daylight area where the sun incinerates everyone stupid enough to wander into the desert, there is a small autonomous mining operation producing and enriching uranium. Anyhow, after yet another dominator attack on our system we discovered a kelleroid expedition in the daylight zone that was closely "scrutinizing" our high-tech production rigs. I don't think I need to explain what may happen if dominators lay their hands on a supply of enriched uranium. Oh, all right, let me spell it out: they will blow our entire planet to smithereens with their damn nukes! Unless, of course, you can stop them. Think about all those untold millions of relatively innocent civilians and cute babies that will perish if you, ranger, refuse to help us. No? Hitting no nerves? Then think about the big fat zeros we will add to your bank account.
69.GovTextWin: Excellent work, <Player>! One can say you have saved our planet from impending doom. What a great stroke of luck it was that you happened upon our planet when you did. We will be in your debt forever. By the way, we could partially repay it right away with <Money> cr for the operation you have conducted so brilliantly.
69.Name: Zenith
69.RobotsLoss: What a mess! Now we only have one last option left! All right, we will activate plan Z right away. Get off the island immediately before we incinerate it from the orbit. A search and rescue whirlybird has already been sent for you.
RobotsStart: Ah, there you are, <Player>! I have to tell you that there have been numerous prior attempts to retake Zenith, so as you can see the island has morphed into a well-fortified battlefield with all its anti-tank hedgehogs, forts, fortified hills, etc. We even hired a couple of rangers to conduct low-level bombing sorties, but one of them quit almost immediately, and the other... ...didn't quite make it to quitting. We were even thinking about incinerating the island from the orbit but decided against it before it was too late since it turns out local "water," if you can call it that, emits poisonous fumes when sufficiently heated, and the winds may blow them all the way to the twilight zone soon enough.

Strictly speaking, there is no need to defeat the kelleroids. All you have to do is <clr>destroy both enrichment centers<clrEnd>, which you simply cannot miss. The first one is located <clr>slightly to the east of your base<clrEnd>, and the second one -- <clr>right next to the kelleroid base<clrEnd>. To destroy an enrichment module, simply shoot it at center point where all power lines come together, or, if this proves to be too complicated, detonate an explosive charge nearby. Good luck!
69.RobotsWin: Excellent! The enrichment modules are destroyed, the enemy is defeated, and victory is ours! By the way, they are already waiting for you at the government building.

70.GovTextLoss: It's too bad, ranger, that you couldn't pull it off, but anyway, thank you for trying. I am going to pay you <Money> cr as compensation for your time and effort. I am afraid it will be the last banking transaction ever conducted on this planet since we are about to declare total evacuation. Experts believe the station may blow up any minute now. The planet may still survive and avoid a complete blowout, but we cannot risk innocent lives expecting a miracle. I don't think you should linger around here either.
GovTextStart: It's good that you asked. There is this one mission, a very important mission as a matter of fact.

You should know that we only use environmentally sound geothermal energy to generate electricity that, among other things, powers the lights and computer screens in this office. Overall, it is about the only energy source on our planet. It is all very simple and easy to use since our planet has a very hot core. The only reason we have not yet all cooked on the surface is that the planet is far enough from the sun to compensate for the extra heat emanated by the core.

All our power plants are located deep underground, which makes perfect sense since the deeper it is, the hotter the magma. Additionally, these plants also produce all kinds of souvenirs and tchotchkes. For example, the shape of this black molten rock somewhat resembles a swarokok ready to leap. See that vicious scowl? And these are the tiny paws. You still don't see it? Come on, ranger, use your imagination. But anyway, we digress.

One of these plants has been taken over by dominators even though we have no idea how they could possibly get there. These iron buggers wasted almost the entire operating crew and then went about their usual dominator business that mostly involves fighting each other. Seriously, like they couldn't find some other place for it! Because of them, the plant's machinery continues to operate with no supervision, which is very dangerous. A small overload here, a short there -- and the entire planet goes kaboom! We may be sitting in our comfortable armchairs now, but in fact we are sitting on a ticking bomb. Be seated, <Player>, be seated. That was a figure of speech. Don't worry, the seat is not going to explode under you.

Ranger, I would like you to take on the important mission of destroying the dominators that have taken over the station. We know that all of you rangers undergo special training, so it looks like of all of us here you are the most qualified person for the job. If you manage to pull it off, you will have the gratitude of our entire population, and I will personally pay you <Money> cr. Provided the planet stays in one piece, that is.
GovTextWin: Phew! To tell you the truth, ranger, you got us worried at some point. But all is well that ends well. A specialist team has already been dispatched to the plant. They will take control of the equipment and put everything in order there. We needn't worry about the debris and remaining robots. Those can simply be dumped into molten magma where they will dissolve without a trace. By the way, that's not a bad way to dispose of any kind of trash. I normally keep a bucket of molten lava under my desk in lieu of a shredder. You just have to be careful not to spill it on your feet, or you may have to do without. But at least no one who has no business reading secret documents will be able to read them.
Thank you, <Player>, your help came in very handy. As promised, I am going to transfer <Money> cr to your account. Use them for a good cause.
70.Name: Core
70.RobotsLoss: You were defeated. There is nothing else we can do now except order mandatory evacuation, and you have to report to the government building right away.
70.RobotsStart: All right, ranger. Just remember not to fire your guns indiscriminately. Take good aim first. If you hit any equipment, the planet may blow before you can say, "Oops, I missed." Your startup resources are all ready, and one of the plants is standing by. You can go ahead now.
70.RobotsWin: Great! Dominators have been defeated! Ranger, you have just saved our entire planet from imminent doom. You can begin making your way out of the station. Try to report to the government building ASAP.
